Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation. OBJECTIVE: To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms. METHODS: A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status. RESULTS: Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV). CONCLUSIONS: Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

recs.title: Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH. METHODS: The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH. RESULTS: No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.78-1.24). In contrast, new-onset PH (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH. CONCLUSIONS: Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

recs.title: Reply to Clinical reflections on the non-Lp(a) apoB/Lp(a) ratio.
Selective blockade of microRNA-31-5p-calcitonin receptor interaction reverses established atrial fibrosis and atrial arrhythmia burden.
recs.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is promoted by atrial fibrosis, a form of structural remodelling for which effective therapies are lacking. MicroRNA-31-5p (miR-31-5p), an aging-associated, atrial-enriched microRNA, has been linked to AF, but its role in atrial fibrosis is unknown. Here we show that atrial fibroblasts from patients with persistent AF exhibit increased miR-31-5p expression and reduced expression of the calcitonin receptor (CTR, encoded by CALCR). MiR-31-5p directly represses CTR and promotes pro-fibrotic fibroblast responses, whereas its inhibition restores CTR expression. Fibroblast-specific overexpression of miR-31 in mice reduces atrial CTR expression, increases atrial fibrosis and enhances arrhythmia susceptibility. Selective disruption of miR-31-5p-CALCR binding using a locked nucleic acid target site blocker restores atrial CTR expression, prevents fibrosis progression and reduces arrhythmia burden. In mice with established atrial remodeling, this strategy promotes fibrosis regression, identifying the miR-31-5p-CTR axis as a potential therapeutic target in AF.

recs.title: Shared Genetics of Hypertension and Preeclampsia Converges on Immune Regulation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension and preeclampsia are clinically distinct, yet biologically related conditions characterized by vascular dysfunction and elevated cardiovascular risk. Although genome-wide association studies have identified loci associated with blood pressure traits and preeclampsia, the functional mechanisms linking shared variants to gene regulation and clinical phenotypes remain unclear. METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for hypertension, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and preeclampsia to identify shared variants (P≤1×10-4). Cis-expression quantitative trait loci analyses were performed in whole blood using RNA sequencing data from 180 Black women. Significant associations (false discovery rate ≤0.05) were evaluated for replication across vascular, metabolic, and endocrine tissues in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Associations between gene expression and blood pressure traits were also assessed. RESULTS: We identified 4792 shared genome-wide association study variants, of which 4663 were tested in expression quantitative trait loci analyses, yielding 1837 significant variant-gene associations across 78 genes. Replication in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project confirmed 645 associations involving 24 genes, many showing cross-tissue regulatory effects. Three genes (C4B, HLA-C, and HLA-DQB1) demonstrated convergent evidence across genome-wide association study, gene regulation, and expression-trait analyses. C4B expression was positively associated with hypertension and systolic blood pressure, while HLA-C showed negative associations with hypertension, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure. HLA-DQB1 expression was specifically associated with diastolic blood pressure, suggesting trait-specific effects. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight immune-related pathways as key mediators linking hypertension and preeclampsia. Integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic data provides a framework for identifying functionally relevant loci and advancing mechanistic insights into cardiometabolic and pregnancy-related disorders.

recs.title: Corrigendum to "ST3GAL1-mediated α-2,3 sialylation restrains CD105-TGFβRII signaling to attenuate EndMT-driven atherosclerosis" [Atherosclerosis 422, (2026), 121927].
Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup. METHODS: We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT. RESULTS: After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO. CONCLUSIONS: AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

recs.title: ROBIN to the Rescue: Balloon Laceration for LVOT Obstruction After Incomplete LAMPOON in Valve-in-Ring TMVR.
The Vein of Marshall Promotes Re-Entry After Pulmonary Vein Reconnection.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia recurrence remains a major limitation of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Pulmonary vein (PV) reconnection and epicardial connections from the left atrium (LA) to the vein of Marshall (VoM) and coronary sinus (CS) in proximity to mitral valve are important contributors. We hypothesized that VoM facilitates arrhythmia induction through interaction with the epicardial region encircled by wide antral circumferential ablation (WACA). OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to systematically evaluate the combined effect of PV reconnection and epicardial VoM connectivity on the occurrence of sustained postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia using in silico models. METHODS: Bilayer biatrial models were constructed from electroanatomical and computed tomographic data of 10 patients with AF. Post-AF electrical remodeling and substrate remodeling following the low voltage area distribution, and left-sided WACA were incorporated. Segments of WACA lesions were sequentially restored to simulate PV reconnection. Three connectivity scenarios were evaluated: intact CS-VoM-LA epicardial connection, CS-LA connection only, and no epicardial connections. Sustained re-entry (>10 seconds) was the primary endpoint, and connectivity conditions were compared using patient-level paired vulnerability. Induction of any arrhythmia, tachycardia cycle length, and stable rotor number were secondary outcomes. RESULTS: Sustained re-entry occurred at 92 of 294 (31.3%) reconnection sites with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity, 37 of 294 (12.6%) with CS-LA connectivity only, and 29 of 294 (9.9%) without epicardial connectivity. Patient-level paired analysis showed 19.9-percentage-point and 22.7-percentage-point higher vulnerability with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity compared with CS-LA connectivity alone (95% CI: 7.1-37.3 percentage points) and no epicardial connectivity (95% CI: 7.4-41.3 percentage points), respectively. Mean tachycardia cycle length in the LA was 258.0 ± 25.7 milliseconds, 255.0 ± 31.4 milliseconds, and 251.0 ± 33.9 milliseconds across the 3 scenarios; the average number of stable rotors was 0.6 ± 0.3, 0.7 ± 0.2, and 0.4 ± 0.2, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The VoM is a critical epicardial driver of arrhythmia after incomplete WACA, underscoring the importance of its targeted ablation.

recs.title: Contemporary Burden, Drivers, and Risk-Factor Control Gaps Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages in US Adults, 2021 to 2023.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome staging integrates adiposity, metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Contemporary national estimates of CKM stage distribution, stage drivers, and treatment gaps are needed to inform implementation of the CKM framework. METHODS: We analyzed adults aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 fasting subsample. CKM stage was assigned hierarchically using American Heart Association CKM staging criteria. We estimated survey-weighted CKM stage prevalence, national population counts, stage-specific drivers, and risk-factor control and treatment gaps across stages 2 through 4. RESULTS: The analytic sample included 2958 adults, representing 245.2 million US adults. Overall, 26.4 million adults (10.8%) were stage 0, 56.8 million (23.2%) stage 1, 125.9 million (51.3%) stage 2, 13.4 million (5.5%) stage 3, and 22.7 million (9.3%) stage 4. Stage ≥1 was present in 89.2%, stage ≥2 in 66.1%, and advanced CKM (stages 3-4) in 14.7%. Among stage 1 adults, 85.1% had adiposity and 49.2% had prediabetes. Among adults with stage 2 CKM, hypertension (72.0%), metabolic syndrome (56.1%), and hypertriglyceridemia (41.9%) were common drivers. Among adults with stage 3 CKM, 95.8% met the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events 10-year cardiovascular disease risk criterion. Risk-factor control and treatment gaps were common across stages 2 through 4, including blood pressure ≥130/80 mm Hg in 50.3% to 66.9%, lipid-lowering therapy nonuse among eligible adults in 30.1% to 59.2%, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol above the target in 64.5% to 73.9%. CONCLUSIONS: CKM syndrome affects most US adults, with stage-specific drivers and persistent risk-factor control and treatment gaps. These findings provide contemporary benchmarks for CKM surveillance and implementation.

A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
recs.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

recs.title: Exercise chronotropic inefficiency in patients with heart failure across distinct left ventricular ejection fraction phenotypes.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To characterize the pattern of chronotropic incompetence (CI) response to exercise in patients with heart failure (HF) across distinct phenotypes of the left ventricular ejection fraction and to explore the extent to which heart rate (HR) response should be prioritized as a therapeutic target within personalized HF management strategies. METHODS: Patients with HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and healthy controls underwent incremental exercise testing with simultaneous gas exchange and echocardiography assessments. Stroke volume (SV), HR, cardiac output (CO), and arteriovenous oxygen difference [C(a-v)O2] were assessed from rest to peak exercise. Graphical analyses explored relationships amongst determinants of oxygen uptake (V̇O2). RESULTS: Both HF phenotypes exhibited CI and a blunted increase in CO during exercise compared with controls. Peak HR was similarly reduced by 20% in HFpEF and 23% in HFrEF. HFpEF, however, exhibited a steeper HR-VO2 relationship. HFrEF demonstrated a greater compensatory increase in peripheral O2 extraction, with peak C(a-v)O2 73% higher than controls and 21% higher than HFpEF. In contrast, HFpEF showed limited ability to augment C(a-v)O2 and presented the lowest relative peak V̇O2 (-39% vs. controls and -16% vs. HFrEF), despite similar peak V̇O2%pred between HF phenotypes. CONCLUSION: CI can contribute to exercise intolerance in both HF phenotypes, with distinct compensatory mechanisms. An integrated cardiopulmonary exercise testing-echocardiography approach may support identifying phenotype-specific physiological profiles that might address therapeutic strategies targeting CI, SV reserve, and peripheral O2 utilization to improve functional capacity in HF. Addressing the kinetics of HR slope and ΔHR metrics seems relevant to implement knowledge on the fundamental CI contribution in HF phenotypes.

Rationale and Design of a Parallel Randomized Trial of a DASH-Enhanced Portfolio Diet With or Without Ultra-Processed Plant Proteins for Blood Pressure and Other Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Adults With Hypertension and Obesity: The Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention on Cardiometabolic Health Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death and hospitalization globally. Clinical practice guidelines recommend various plant-based dietary patterns that target specific cardiometabolic risk factors, including the Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet for blood pressure and the Portfolio diet for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Combining key elements of these patterns may enhance cardiovascular disease risk reduction. However, many soy-based products, a key Portfolio component, are classified as ultra-processed foods (UPFs). This trial will answer 2 questions: (1) Does a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet result in clinically meaningful reductions in blood pressure compared with standard of care and (2) Is a high-UPF noninferior to a low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet for blood pressure reduction? METHODS: The SWITCH (Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention for Cardiometabolic Health) trial is a parallel, randomized, 3-arm, open-label, superiority-noninferiority trial. Three hundred adults with hypertension and obesity, including 50% with type 2 diabetes, will be randomized to a high-UPF or low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet or standard of care for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is systolic blood pressure. Key secondary outcomes are non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and body weight. Other outcomes include cardiometabolic risk factors. CONCLUSIONS: Findings will provide high-quality evidence on the use of a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet and the role of nutrient-dense soy foods classified as UPFs within the combination of the 2 guideline-based dietary patterns to support dietary strategies for cardiometabolic risk reduction. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06907862.

recs.title: Pulmonary vein isolation with a contact force-sensing, large-tip focal pulsed field ablation catheter with 3D mapping for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month results.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05971693) evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact force-sensing, pulsed field ablation basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to report 12-month (12M) study outcomes. METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE catheter. Patients underwent follow-up through the 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness end point was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic or asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 seconds) and acute procedural failure. Device- and/or procedure-related serious adverse events, quality of life assessed using Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life scores, and health care utilization (cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug use) were also evaluated. RESULTS: Of the 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main phase cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic or asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device- and/or procedure-related serious adverse events occurred in 2.9% of main phase patients. The mean overall Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-related hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% compared with the 12M preprocedure period, and class I or III antiarrhythmic drug use decreased by 49.3% from baseline to 6-12M postablation. CONCLUSION: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and health care benefits of pulsed field ablation with the OMNYPULSE catheter. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05971693.

recs.title: Cardiovascular and metabolic acute effects of heated tobacco products in healthy smokers.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) are increasingly promoted as 'reduced-harm' alternatives to combustible cigarettes, despite delivering pharmacologically active nicotine and complex aerosols. Independent human data on their acute cardiovascular effects remain limited. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this investigator-initiated, within-subject pre-post study, healthy adult smokers were supervised in their exposure to two consecutive HTP sticks (IQOS). Endothelial function was assessed by brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD), along with haemodynamic parameters, venous blood gas and metabolic markers, and oxidative DNA damage measured by the comet assay. Acute HTP exposure resulted in a significant reduction in FMD, indicating rapid endothelial dysfunction. This was accompanied by an increase in systolic blood pressure, reductions in venous oxygen tension and saturation, and an increase in venous carbon dioxide, consistent with impaired tissue oxygenation. Methaemoglobin levels increased, reflecting oxidative modification of haemoglobin, while metabolic alterations in glucose and lactate suggested nicotine-mediated sympathetic and metabolic stress. Importantly, short-term HTP use induced significant oxidative DNA damage in peripheral blood cells. These effects occurred after a single, real-world exposure in otherwise healthy smokers. CONCLUSION: Together, these findings demonstrate that HTPs are not biologically inert and that acute exposure is sufficient to trigger vascular dysfunction, systemic metabolic disturbance, and genotoxic stress. The results challenge claims of cardiovascular harm reduction and underscore that all nicotine-containing products remain relevant targets for cardiovascular prevention and regulation.

recs.title: Anatomical Insight Into Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Papillary Muscles.
recs.abstract: The papillary muscles (PAMs) are important sites of origin of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs). Although catheter ablation of idiopathic PAM VAs has proven to be an effective treatment, these arrhythmias remain challenging compared with other idiopathic VAs despite advances in technologies and techniques. This is related to the unique anatomical challenges of these structures. PAMs are anatomically unique in their location, morphology, histologic composition, and connections with surrounding structures. Electrophysiological studies and catheter ablation of PAM VAs have revealed specific electrocardiographic and electrophysiological characteristics of idiopathic PAM VAs, such as inconsistent precordial transition, discordant QRS axis, multiform VA morphologies, and preferential conduction. Anatomical studies with the aid of imaging modalities, such as intracardiac echocardiography, computed tomography, and cardiac magnetic resonance, have helped define the anatomical background underlying these electrocardiographic and electrophysiological characteristics. This article reviews the unique anatomy of PAMs from an electrophysiological standpoint to better understand the anatomy of the PAMs and thereby improve the outcomes of catheter ablation of idiopathic PAM VAs.

recs.title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
recs.abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

recs.title: A New Frontier in Heart Failure: Promise and Pitfalls of Primary Prevention.
Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

recs.title: VSMC DDR1 Mechanosensation Aggravates Atherosclerosis via Paracrine Signaling.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases cardiovascular risk and is linked to arterial stiffening and atherosclerosis. How stiffness promotes atherogenesis remains unclear. DDR1 (discoidin domain receptor 1), a mechanosensory tyrosine kinase receptor, has been implicated in force-regulated arterial remodeling. We investigated whether DDR1-mediated mechanosensation links arterial stiffness to vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC)-endothelial paracrine communication in CKD-related atherosclerosis. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, secretome proteomics, and bulk RNA sequencing were integrated with stiffness-controlled models, endothelial assays, and a CKD-hyperlipidemia mouse model. SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion and a DDR1 dephosphorylation-targeting chimera (DEPTAC) were evaluated in vivo. Plasma TSP-1 (thrombospondin-1) levels were quantified in a CKD clinical cohort and analyzed in relation to renal function and atherosclerosis severity. RESULTS: CKD-associated vascular stiffening coincided with SMC phenotypic switching and enhanced THBS signaling. Multiomics integration identified THBS1 as a stiffness-induced SMC secretory effector. Stiff matrices increased SMC THBS1 secretion, promoting endothelial proliferation, migration, and leukocyte adhesion; these effects were attenuated by THBS1 knockdown. DDR1 coupled matrix stiffness cues to THBS1 expression by regulating its transcription via a tyrosine 3-monooxygenase/tryptophan 5-monooxygenase activation protein epsilon-FOXO3 (forkhead box O3) axis. Vascular SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion reduced aortic THBS1 levels, vascular stiffening, and atherosclerotic burden. DEPTAC suppressed aberrant DDR1 phosphorylation, reduced THBS1, and ameliorated vascular stiffening and atherosclerosis. Plasma THBS1 increased with CKD severity and correlated with atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: DDR1-dependent mechanosensing in SMCs drives stiffness-induced paracrine signaling to endothelium via THBS1, promoting CKD-accelerated atherosclerosis. Targeting mechanical DDR1 activation may be therapeutic.

Depressive Symptoms and 6-Year KCCQ Health Status in Chronic Heart Failure: Findings From the Cognition.Matters-HF Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term disease-specific health status trajectories in ambulatory chronic heart failure (HF) are incompletely characterized, and the contribution of depressive symptoms remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize 6-year Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OSS) trajectories and distinguish persistent and visit-specific depressive symptom associations with health status. METHODS: In the prospective Cognition.Matters-HF cohort, 148 patients with HF underwent assessments at baseline and 6, 12, 36, and 69 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated KCCQ-OSS trajectories and prespecified correlates. Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores were decomposed into between-person and within-person components. Sensitivity analyses addressed missingness, and exploratory lagged analyses assessed whether recent PHQ-9 worsening predicted subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events. RESULTS: KCCQ-OSS remained stable over 69 months (78.0-76.6; change: -1.4; 95% CI: -4.6 to 1.8; P for time = 0.065), despite substantial individual variation. Higher between-person PHQ-9 burden (β: -3.44 per point; 95% CI: -4.00 to -2.88; P < 0.001) and within-person PHQ-9 worsening (β: -1.80; 95% CI: -2.50 to -1.11; P < 0.001) were associated with lower concurrent KCCQ-OSS. Recent PHQ-9 worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ-OSS, a ≥5-point KCCQ decline, or all-cause death/HF hospitalization. NYHA functional class and 6-min walking distance, but not N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, left ventricular ejection fraction, or executive function, were independently associated with KCCQ-OSS. CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory chronic HF, average KCCQ-based health status remained stable over 6 years despite substantial individual variation. Depressive symptoms were strongly associated with concurrent health status, but recent worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.

Left bundle branch pacing vs left ventricular septal pacing in the same patients with heart failure and left bundle branch block.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) are considered to be acceptable as left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) strategies. The differences in cardiac mechanical performance between LBBP and LVSP in the same patients with heart failure (HF) and left bundle branch block (LBBB) are yet to be determined. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to compare mechanical function and resynchronization effect of LBBP and LVSP as CRTP modalities. METHODS: Fourteen patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and typical complete LBBB who received cardiac resynchronization therapy pacing (CRTP) implantation were enrolled. All patient implantation with two ventricular pacing leads, enabling both LBBP and LVSP. Acute cardiac function and resynchronization effect were assessed by echocardiography and electrocardiography to compare the differences in LBBB mode, LBBP mode, and LVSP mode within the same patients undergoing CRTP. RESULTS: Both pacing modes significantly reduced QRS duration (QRSd) and left ventricular activation time (LVAT) versus LBBB (all P<0.001), with LVSP yielding wider QRSd than LBBP (P<0.001). LBBP showed better performance in LV mechanical synchrony parameter (SDI) than LVSP, and both pacing modes were superior to that of LBBB condition (all P < 0.001). LVEF increased significantly with both pacing modes, with a greater increase observed in LBBP compared to LVSP. No significant differences in right ventricular function were observed among the three modes. CONCLUSION: In this pilot study of patients with HF and LBBB, both LBBP and LVSP significantly improved left ventricular hemodynamics and mechanical synchrony without compromising RV function. LBBP potentially has superior left ventricular hemodynamic effects to LVSP.

Transvenous Lead Extraction Without Dedicated Surgical Back up in Low-Risk Patients.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) is associated with major complications that could require immediate surgical rescue. These procedures are performed in an EP lab or hybrid OR with the presence of a surgical team on standby. We have designed an institutional protocol that permits performance of TLE in low-risk situations, in an EP lab without dedicated surgical back-up. OBJECTIVES: To investigate outcomes of TLE in low-risk patients METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients who underwent low-risk TLE at Emory Healthcare between 2010-23. Low-risk TLE were defined as an extraction of a pacing or ICD lead with a dwell time >= 1 and <= 5 years or a lead < 1 year that required extraction tools. RESULTS: Among 482 patients who met the criteria, the average lead age was 2.8 ± 1.2 years. The mean number of targeted leads per patient was 1.6±0.7. Extraction tools were required in 33.1% of cases. Major complications occurred in 0.83% of patients (n=4): 2 pericardial effusions requiring pericardiocentesis, 1 pneumothorax and 1 death from cardiogenic shock in an end stage heart failure patient. The patients with pericardial effusions and pneumothorax were part of a procedure that required lead revisions and the insertion of 1 or more new leads. No patients required surgical rescue. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that, in selected "low-risk" patients, TLE can be performed safely in an experienced EP lab at centers with on-site cardiac surgery but without a dedicated surgical standby team, potentially reducing resource utilization in resource-limited healthcare environments.

Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated. OBJECTIVE: To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%. RESULTS: Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort. CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

recs.title: The evolution and future of conduction system pacing.
recs.abstract: Cardiac pacing has undergone a fundamental paradigm shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system of the heart. Decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing, which engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart, has emerged as a transformative approach that preserves or restores the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form of conduction system pacing, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability: from management of bradycardia and prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is an emerging atrial counterpart: by capturing a preferential interatrial conduction pathway, this approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. Bachmann bundle area pacing might, therefore, help to prevent atrial fibrillation. In this Review, we bring these ventricular and atrial strategies together under the unifying principle of physiological pacing, describe their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraise the latest evidence from randomized trials and address the practical questions that arise in clinical application, indicating where more evidence is required.

recs.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. METHODS: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment. FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group. INTERPRETATION: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended. FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

recs.title: Baseline gradient, valve morphology and left ventricular recovery and survival after TAVR in reduced-ejection-fraction aortic stenosis: a retrospective cohort study.
Assessment and Reversibility of Hepatic Abnormalities in Heart Failure: Liver in Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: Hepatic abnormalities in non-Fontan heart failure result from congestive hepatopathy and hypoperfusion-related ischemic injury, compounded by neurohormonal activation and systemic inflammation. Assessment of liver disease severity is challenging because standard liver biochemistries, serum fibrosis markers, severity score models, elastography, and imaging modalities have limited diagnostic accuracy in congestive hepatopathy, and hepatic fibrosis is often heterogeneous on histology in this population. Management focuses on optimization of cardiac function through medical therapy or mechanical circulatory support. Although liver biochemical abnormalities frequently improve with restoration of cardiac function, histologic reversibility is variable and not consistently observed. In patients with advanced heart failure needing heart transplantation, histologic cirrhosis and/or fibrosis accompanied by portal hypertension may merit consideration of combined heart-liver transplantation, but correlation between fibrosis and clinical outcomes varies. There remains an unmet need for tests that can reliably assess liver disease severity and predict liver outcomes in non-Fontan congestive hepatopathy.

recs.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Coronary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis. CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.

recs.title: Angiography-Derived Radial Wall Strain Across All Epicardial Vessels Before Acute Coronary Syndrome: The CULPRIT-STRAIN Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiography-derived radial wall strain (RWS) is a biomechanical index associated with plaque vulnerability. Whether elevated RWS demonstrates culprit-vessel predominance or broader multivessel distribution within the same patient is unknown. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare maximal RWS (RWSmax) in the future culprit vessel with nonculprit vessels within the same patient and assess its association with time to acute coronary syndrome (ACS). METHODS: In the multicenter CULPRIT-STRAIN study, consecutive ACS patients with a prior coronary angiogram (≥3 months before event) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry (NCT04185285). RWSmax was measured in all 3 epicardial coronary arteries at the index angiogram. The primary endpoint was within-patient comparison of culprit vs nonculprit RWSmax; secondary endpoints included its association with index-to-ACS interval and the prevalence of multivessel biomechanical elevation. RESULTS: Among 101 patients (303 vessels; median index-to-ACS interval, 35 months), culprit-vessel RWSmax was higher than nonculprit-vessel RWSmax (19.7% vs 11.3%; P < 0.001). The culprit vessel had the highest RWSmax in 96 patients (95.0%; P < 0.001), with a median within-patient ΔRWS of 7.0% (IQR: 3.6%-13.2%). In exploratory analysis, higher culprit-vessel RWSmax was associated with a shorter index-to-ACS interval (ρ = -0.34; P < 0.001). Overall, 60.4% of patients had ≥2 vessels with RWSmax >12%. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who developed ACS, RWSmax demonstrated marked culprit-vessel predominance despite frequent multivessel elevation, indicating a graded distribution across vessels. These retrospective findings do not establish prospective risk prediction and require validation in unselected populations with event-free controls.

recs.title: Prognostic Significance of Plasma Lactate Levels in Postcardiotomy Patients.
Pulsed Field Ablation of the Left Atrial Appendage Before Mechanical Closure to Reduce Peri-Device Leak (STUN-AF).
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (LAAC) is plagued by late peri-device leak. We posited that appendage contraction prevents full LAA seal, so conversely, LAA stunning with pulsed field ablation (PFA) of the LAA (left atrial appendage ablation [LAAA]) might promote rapid appendage thrombosis/obliteration. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to assess the impact of LAAA during concomitant procedures on eliminating leaks. METHODS: At 3 centers, consecutive patients undergoing concomitant PFA and LAAC also underwent LAAA or did not undergo LAAA, at operator discretion. Initial (∼3-4 months) (29% transesophageal echocardiography/71% computed tomography) and 12-month imaging were compared with a primary composite outcome of LAA patency, defined as either detectable flow into the LAA or evidence of echo-free space/contrast medium behind the device. RESULTS: Among 317 total patients undergoing PFA and LAAC, including 222 patients who underwent LAAA and 95 who did not (control patients), all underwent initial imaging and 126 reached 12-month imaging follow-up. Device compression was 28% with LAAA vs 25% without LAAA (P < 0.001). Implantation success was 100%. The periprocedural adverse event rate was 2% in both groups. The primary composite outcome of LAA patency was significantly reduced with LAAA vs no-LAAA, both at 3-4 months (29% vs 64%; P < 0.001) and at 12 months (4% vs 42%; P < 0.001). Device-related thrombus rates were low and similar (2.3% vs 3.2%; P = 0.7). A validation subset including only patients with alternating LAAA assignment (LAAA: n = 59; no-LAAA: n = 63) again revealed that LAAA was associated with reduced LAA patency (3-4 months: 34% vs 51%; P = 0.06; 12 months: 8% vs 36%; P = 0.2). Final LAA e' velocity was significantly different between groups (17 ± 7 vs 34 ± 16 cm/s; P < 0.001), with higher velocity associated with LAA patency (P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: PFA of the LAA has potential to reduce LAA patency during device-based LAAC.

recs.title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI-1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood. METHODS: Six-week-old male wild-type (PAI-1+/+) and PAI-1 knockout (PAI-1-/-) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI-1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI-1 levels. PAI-1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac-specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI-1 deletion. In vitro, PAI-1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI-1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI-1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI-1 silencing. CONCLUSIONS: PAI-1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte-associated function of PAI-1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI-1-JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.

recs.title: Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions: Detection Is No Longer Diagnosis.
recs.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America. OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort. METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years. RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027. CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

Weekly Journal Scan: rethinking factor XIa inhibition after acute coronary syndromes.
Effects of Walnut Consumption on Anti-MDA-LDL Antibodies and Immunoglobulins in the WAHA Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Higher total serum IgG levels have been associated with protection from cardiovascular events in ASCOT (Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial). Antibodies against oxidized low-density lipoprotein (LDL) have also been linked to favorable clinical and vascular imaging outcomes. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to determine whether regular walnut consumption influences circulating immunoglobulins, malondialdehyde-modified LDL (MDA-LDL), a highly immunogenic form of oxidized LDL, and antibodies against MDA-LDL. METHODS: The Walnuts and Healthy Aging study was a two-center, randomized controlled trial conducted in Spain and the United States. Adults aged 63 to 79 years were assigned to a walnut-enriched diet or a control diet excluding walnuts for 2 years. Serum total immunoglobulin G (IgG), total immunoglobulin M (IgM), MDA-LDL, and IgG and IgM anti MDA-LDL antibodies were measured by enzyme-linked immunoassays in 474 participants. RESULTS: Baseline immunoglobulin concentrations differed substantially by study center. Participants from the United States had 25% lower total IgM and IgG concentrations than participants from Spain. Walnut consumption increased total serum IgG by 11% in the U.S. cohort (95% CI: 0%-24%; P = 0.040), whereas pooled analysis showed a 6% increase across both cohorts (95% CI: 0%-12%; P = 0.041). Over the 2-year study period, total IgM and both IgG and IgM anti-MDA-LDL concentrations declined significantly in both the control and intervention groups. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term walnut consumption was associated with a modest increase in total serum IgG but had no significant effect on total IgM, MDA-LDL, or antibodies against MDA-LDL. Baseline IgG and IgM concentrations were substantially lower among U.S. participants, suggesting that geographic, environmental, social, or genetic factors may modulate immune biomarkers independently of dietary intervention.

recs.title: When platelets are under pressure: an angiotensin II-TGF-β axis in hypertensive patients leads to receptor PAR4 overexpression.
Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT. METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT). RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients. CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

recs.title: Women's Cardiovascular Health: From Recognition to Action.
Pulsed field ablation: from concepts to technology.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a transformative approach for treating cardiac arrhythmias by exploiting irreversible electroporation to preferentially injure myocardium while limiting collateral damage. Translating this biophysical principle into safe and effective clinical systems requires careful integration of waveform design, catheter engineering, computational and experimental modelling, safety testing, and procedural workflow. OBJECTIVE: This review summarizes the fundamental physical and engineering principles that govern cardiac PFA and examines how these principles influence efficacy, safety, lesion formation, and clinical usability. BIOPHYSICAL AND TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS: Electroporation is governed primarily by the local electric field and waveform-dependent lethal thresholds rather than generator voltage alone. Key waveform variables include monophasic vs. biphasic pulses, microsecond vs. nanosecond pulse widths, duty cycle, and total application duration. Catheter design further determines electric field distribution, lesion geometry, current density, and applicability across anatomic targets, with important distinctions between bipolar and monopolar configurations. MODELLING AND SAFETY: Experimental and computational approaches used to investigate PFA include finite element simulations, cell culture systems, vegetal substrates, and in vivo animal models, each with distinct strengths and limitations. High-voltage pulse delivery can also produce unintended effects, including Joule heating, electrochemical reactions, bubble formation, arcing, and interactions with implanted electronic devices. These phenomena highlight the importance of optimized waveform design, electrode configuration, and safety monitoring. CLINICAL USABILITY: Clinical adoption depends not only on biological efficacy and safety but also on workflow efficiency, catheter versatility, procedure duration, mapping integration, anaesthesia requirements, and adaptability to differing clinical practices and geographic settings. CONCLUSIONS: The performance of a PFA system reflects the interaction of biophysics, waveform characteristics, catheter design, modelling, safety controls, and procedural usability. Understanding these interconnected principles is essential for developing PFA technologies that are effective, safe, predictable, and practical for contemporary electrophysiology laboratories.

recs.title: T-Cell-Derived IFNγ Instructs ECM Crosslinking by Cardiac Fibroblasts Through LOXL3 in Experimental Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a major clinical challenge characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Left ventricular stiffening and inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF, yet the contribution of ECM (extracellular matrix) stiffness and the immune-stromal mechanisms driving ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF remain poorly understood. METHODS: We used the murine 2-hit model of cardiometabolic HFpEF, in which the combination of high-fat diet and hypertension induced by L-nitro-arginine-methyl ester causes diastolic dysfunction. We evaluated diastolic function by echocardiography and ECM mechanics by uniaxial tensile testing of decellularized cardiac tissue. Functional in vivo studies included genetic depletion of T cells, IFNγ (interferon-γ) knockout mice, and pharmacological lysyl oxidase inhibition. We combined cocultures of CD4+ T cells and cardiac fibroblasts with mechanical testing of cardiac ECM and molecular biology to elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Left ventricular ECM stiffness strongly correlated with impaired diastolic function in experimental cardiometabolic HFpEF. Cardiac CD4+ T-cell infiltration was required for ECM stiffening and upregulation of lysyl oxidase enzymes in cardiac fibroblast. We discovered that CD4+ T-cell-derived IFNγ was required to induce LOXL3 in cardiac fibroblast, which increased ECM stiffness in vitro. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that a signaling axis involving IFNγ, PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase), AKT, and HIF1α (hypoxia-inducible factor-1α) drives LOXL3 expression and subsequent collagen crosslinking. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of this IFNγ-HIF1α-LOXL3 axis attenuated adverse ECM remodeling and improved diastolic function. CONCLUSIONS: CD4+ T cells promote pathological ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF through IFNγ-mediated, cardiac fibroblast LOXL3-dependent ECM crosslinking. Targeting this immune-stromal pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for HFpEF.

Plasma Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme as a Prioritized Candidate Target for Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence From Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: We aimed to provide hypothesis-generating evidence on druggable targets for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) with evidence from a conventional observational analysis of drug use in a large prospective cohort. METHODS: Proteome-wide MR analysis was conducted to identify plasma proteins causally related to AD risk using the largest summary-level data to date, followed by colocalization and multiomic validation analyses (on the gene expression, alternative splicing, and DNA methylation levels in blood and brain, respectively) to prioritize potential druggable targets. We also replicated our MR findings using additional genetic data and performed multivariable MR for the prioritized findings. Conventional observational analysis in UK Biobank, a large prospective cohort, was performed to provide further clinical implications, using active comparator to minimize confounding by indication. RESULTS: MR analysis identified 15 plasma proteins with putative causal effects on AD risk. Of them, inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme was found to increase the risk of AD (odds ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 1.08-1.14]), which was likely independent of blood pressure as suggested by multivariable MR. Observational analysis in UK Biobank showed a higher incidence (hazard ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.00-1.50]) of AD among regular users of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, compared with the active comparator angiotensin receptor blocker users. CONCLUSIONS: Our genetic analyses prioritized angiotensin-converting enzyme as a candidate target, and a conventional observational analysis in a large prospective cohort provided supportive evidence that regular angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor use was associated with a higher AD risk, which needs further investigation with high-quality real-world evidence and clinical trials before being translated into practice changes.

Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion. METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. RESULTS: Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06]; P=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09]; P=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage.
