Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency. METHODS: In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs. RESULTS: Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%). CONCLUSION: Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

recs.title: A REBIRTH of Disease-Specific Therapy: Will Targeting Prolactin Reshape Treatment of Peripartum Cardiomyopathy?
Residual Risk From Remnant Cholesterol and Inflammation Despite Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Association With Incident Peripheral Artery Disease in Type 2 Diabetes.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy, patients with type 2 diabetes retain a significant residual risk for peripheral artery disease (PAD). The contributions of remnant cholesterol (RC) and systemic inflammation in this treated population, particularly beyond achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, remain incompletely understood. METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 18 741 participants with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank who were free of PAD and were on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline. Plasma RC and hsCRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) levels were measured at baseline. Incident PAD was ascertained over a median follow-up of 13.6 years. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios after adjustment for demographic, clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related covariates, including low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and baseline coronary artery disease. RESULTS: During follow-up, incident PAD occurred in 1223 participants (6.5%). Elevated RC and hsCRP levels were each independently linked to an increased risk of PAD. Participants with concurrent elevations in both RC and hsCRP exhibited the highest risk of incident PAD. These associations remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of participants with baseline coronary artery disease, removal of events within the initial 2-year follow-up, elimination of individuals with hsCRP >10 mg/L, competing-risk analyses accounting for death, and further adjustment for detailed lipid-lowering therapy categories. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention of PAD, elevated RC and systemic inflammation are independently and jointly associated with future PAD risk. These findings highlight substantial residual risk beyond managed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and support the need for further strategies targeting both remnant lipoproteins and inflammation in this high-risk population.

Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood. METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts. RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

recs.title: Integrative Genomic Analyses Identify Collagen Type XXI Alpha 1 Chain and ENPEP-Fibroblast Growth Factor 5 Regulatory Pathways for Blood Pressure Variation in East Asian People.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension and diabetes are common cardiometabolic disorders that may share genetic and environmental risk factors. However, the regulatory genes and tissue-specific mechanisms underlying blood pressure variations remain incompletely understood. METHODS: Leveraging a well-characterized prospective population-based cohort comprised of 27 308 participants from the SCHS (Singapore Chinese Health Study), we evaluated genome-wide genetic associations for 5 blood pressure traits: hypertension status, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure and pulse pressure. Additionally, we conducted a transcriptome-wide association study, integrating gene expression data from 49 tissues, followed by colocalization and fine-mapping to prioritize regulatory genes. Association of identified variants with incident diabetes was additionally evaluated in the longitudinal data. RESULTS: We validated 10 blood pressure loci (P between 1.64×10-20-4.10×10-8) and identified an East Asian-specific splice donor variant at the COL21A1 gene associated with pulse pressure (rs149344559, P=6.78×10-10). Integrative analyses prioritized FGF5 in kidney cortex and ENPEP in pituitary tissue as candidate regulatory genes. The blood pressure-lowering allele at ENPEP (T allele, rs1879056) was associated with reduced risk of incident diabetes. Mediation analysis demonstrated that ∼20.1% of the genetic association with diabetes was mediated through mean arterial pressure (Pindirect-effect<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This study refines genetic predispositions for blood pressure among East Asian individuals. We further delineate tissue-specific regulatory pathways underlying blood pressure variations and identify ENPEP-mediated dysfunctions linking blood pressure genetics to diabetes risk, underscoring integrated disease mechanisms.

recs.title: Targeted Transcatheter Mitral Edge-to-Edge Repair for Dynamic Systolic Anterior Motion After Mitral Valve Repair.
Correction to: Effectiveness of Nurse-Coordinated, Digital-Supported Collaborative Care Model in Reducing Hospital Stay and Mortality Among Patients With Heart Failure: TIME-HF Cluster RCT India.
Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
recs.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

recs.title: Intersection of Patient and Hospital Rurality in Heart Failure Care and Outcomes.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Rural-urban disparities in heart failure (HF) care delivery and outcomes are well documented. However, it remains unclear if differences in outcomes after HF hospitalization are primarily driven by patient rural residence, hospital resources, or both. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of patient and hospital rurality with quality of care and postdischarge outcomes after hospitalization for HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries in US hospitals with HFrEF with an index hospitalization from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2021. Included were Medicare beneficiaries discharged alive after an index hospitalization for HFrEF. Participants were classified as rural patients hospitalized in rural hospitals (rural-rural), rural patients in urban hospitals (rural-urban), urban patients in urban hospitals (urban-urban), and urban patients in rural hospitals (urban-rural). Study data were analyzed from July to September 2026. EXPOSURES: Patient rural residence and hospital rurality. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality after hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included inpatient cardiology consultation, 90-day postdischarge guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use based on prescription fills, and HF readmission at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. RESULTS: Among 735 460 beneficiaries (median [IQR] age, 77 [70-85] years; 415 077 male [56.4%]), 69 061 (9.4%) were rural-rural, 65 510 (8.9%) rural-urban, 582 947 (79.3%) urban-urban, and 17 942 (2.4%) urban-rural. Compared with rural patients treated in rural hospitals, rural patients treated in urban hospitals were more likely to receive inpatient cardiology consultation (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.84-2.22) and initiation of several GDMT classes, including β-blockers (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.16-1.25), ARNIs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.13-1.34), MRAs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.15-1.31), and SGLT2Is (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.32-1.67). They also had lower rates of HF readmission and mortality at all time points (HF readmission 1-year: OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.88; mortality 1-year: OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.89-0.94) than rural-rural patients. Compared with urban patients hospitalized at urban hospitals, rural patients hospitalized at urban hospitals more often received inpatient cardiology consultation (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.31-1.44), whereas postdischarge GDMT differences were modest (absolute difference in GDMT score 0.09 points; 95% CI, 0.05-0.14). Rural patients also had lower HF readmission (1-year OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79-0.82) but higher 30- and 90-day mortality than urban patients (30-day OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; 90-day OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results suggest that hospital rurality was associated with lower odds of GDMT use and higher rates of all-cause mortality, whereas rural residence was associated with mortality differences despite treatment in urban hospitals. Interventions addressing both inpatient resource disparities and postdischarge transitions of care may reduce rural-urban inequities in HF outcomes.

recs.title: Managing Ketogenic Diet-Induced Hypercholesterolemia.
Computational Modeling Reduces Leaflet Modification Rates in Valve-In-Valve and Redo Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary obstruction (CO) complicates valve-in-valve (ViV) and redo transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) at higher rates than native TAVR. Leaflet modification mitigates this risk but increases procedural burden. Traditional computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based risk stratification relies on static parameters that may overestimate risk; computational predictive modeling (CPM) uses patient-specific data to refine risk assessment. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to characterize leaflet modification rates in conventional ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR and evaluate the impact of CPM preprocedural planning augmentation on leaflet modification rates. METHODS: A total of 157 consecutive ViV TAVR or redo-TAVR patients treated from 2022 to 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. CO risk status was derived from traditional CTA parameters. Leaflet modification rates among CTA high-risk subgroups (non-CPM, n = 62; and CPM, n = 29) were compared using Boschloo's one-sided exact test. CPM risk-reclassification patterns were studied using counterfactual binomial analysis. RESULTS: Leaflet modification occurred in 26.3% of ViV TAVR and 24.1% of redo-TAVR procedures that used only conventional CTA-based planning methods. Among patients deemed high risk for CO by conventional methods, leaflet modification was significantly lower in the CPM-augmented subgroup vs that in the non-CPM subgroup (24.1% vs 46.8%; OR: 2.76; 95% CI: 1.03-7.40; P = 0.021). CPM-augmented planning reclassified 82.8% of patients to low-risk status, and 79.2% of reclassified patients were managed without leaflet modification. No COs occurred during the study period. CONCLUSIONS: Among ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR patients at high risk of CO based on conventional CTA-based planning, the use of CPM to augment standard risk assessment was associated with a significant reduction in leaflet modification procedures.

recs.title: Imaging-guided anticoagulation in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: testing the strategy, defining its limits.
Norepinephrine Equivalent Dose for Mortality Risk Stratification in VA-ECMO Cardiogenic Shock.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) complicated by vasoplegia requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) often need escalating vasopressor support and face high mortality. Norepinephrine equivalent dose (NEE) quantifies vasopressor burden, yet its prognostic value in VA-ECMO remains undefined. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship between NEE and 30-day mortality, identify a clinically relevant NEE threshold, and determine factors associated with high vasopressor burden. METHODS: This bicentric retrospective study included 572 consecutive patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO. We collected vasopressor regimens, NEE trajectories, and hemodynamic parameters at predefined intervals. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response linearity. Maximally selected rank statistics with bootstrap validation identified optimal thresholds. Cox models estimated mortality risk. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with high vasopressor burden. RESULTS: The median NEE at ECMO initiation was 0.30 (IQR: 0.09-0.72) μg·kg-1·min-1; 86.2% received norepinephrine. NEE showed a linear dose-response with mortality (HR: 1.06 per 0.1 μg·kg-1·min-1 increment; 95% CI: 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001). A threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 identified high vasopressor burden with elevated 30-day mortality (61.8% vs 42.6%; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.11-1.81; P = 0.005). Factors associated with high vasopressor burden included mechanical ventilation (OR: 2.96; 95% CI: 1.08-8.07), prior epinephrine use (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.12-3.14), renal replacement therapy before VA-ECMO (OR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.02-3.03), baseline lactate (OR: 1.05 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 1.01-1.09), and lower Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score (OR: 0.96 per point; 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Left ventricular unloading was inversely associated (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.34-0.87). CONCLUSIONS: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

recs.title: Reproducible haemodynamics, unresolved indication: where does thrombectomy for acute pulmonary embolism stand?
BAFF Bridge Linking Lupus Autoimmunity to Pulmonary Vascular Damage.
Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling. The proportion of deaths attributable to CVD and CHD across CAC groups was evaluated. Four institutions across the US provided patient-level data to assemble the CAC Consortium. Included in the analysis were adults aged 30 to 45 years from the CAC Consortium. They were followed up for a median of 22.6 years. Study data were analyzed from October 2025 to September 2026. EXPOSURE: Elevated CAC in adults aged 30 to 45 years, specifically CAC score greater than 90%. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Participants were followed up for underlying cause of mortality. RESULTS: Among 12 847 participants, the mean (SD) age was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 (77.2%) were male; 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% to 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. In total, there were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs CAC score of 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27), 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82), and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16), for all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, respectively. Over 30 years, the group with a CAC score greater than 90% had significantly higher modeled risk of all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%), and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality, compared with the group with a CAC score of 0. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study suggest that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

recs.title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany). METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant. CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

recs.title: Correction to: Mechanosensitive Endothelial METTL7A Regulates Internal m7G mRNA Methylation and Protects Against Atherosclerosis.
Coronary micro- and nanoplastics in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: antecedent exposure or post-thrombotic enrichment?
Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04864145.

recs.title: Transcriptomics Identifies a Small Set of Circulating Biomarkers and Signaling Pathways Dysregulated in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: It is sometimes challenging to distinguish hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) from other cardiomyopathies with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). At present, no circulating biomarkers to distinguish HCM have been established. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to identify plasma microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers unique to HCM. METHODS: In this multicenter case-control study, the authors performed comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling in cases with HCM and controls with hypertensive LVH, transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), and aortic stenosis (AS). For each disease group, they chronologically split the patients into training and test sets. The authors identified miRNAs that were significantly (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05) upregulated or downregulated in HCM compared with hypertensive LVH. They made the same comparisons between HCM and ATTR-CM and between HCM and AS. They determined miRNAs that were consistently upregulated or downregulated in HCM throughout all 3 comparisons. Then, they selected miRNAs independently associated with HCM after adjusting for potential confounders. Using the selected miRNAs, the authors developed a logistic regression model to distinguish HCM in the training set. They calculated the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve in the test set. RESULTS: The authors analyzed 2,656 miRNAs in patients with HCM (n = 294), hypertensive LVH (n = 321), ATTR-CM (n = 167), and AS (n = 38). They identified 3 miRNAs (miR-454-3p, miR-98-5p, and miR-5581-3p). The logistic regression model using the 3 miRNAs had an area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.93-0.97) with a sensitivity of 0.95 and a specificity of 0.90 in the test set. CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive plasma transcriptomics profiling identified a small set of circulating miRNAs to distinguish HCM from other cardiomyopathies with LVH.

recs.title: Pulsed Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Glutaminolysis Shapes Cardiac Resilience to Stress via Mitochondrial Glutathione.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac reserve is a strong predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable the heart to mount an adaptive response to stress remain poorly understood. In this study, we sought to dissect the specific role of glutaminolysis, a key anaplerotic and redox-supporting pathway, in regulating cardiac reserve. METHODS: Cardiac reserve was assessed by echocardiography under β-adrenergic stimulation in mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase and in wild-type controls. Stable isotope tracing with [U-13C] glutamine was performed in Langendorff-perfused hearts. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of acute glutamine supplementation in healthy volunteers was conducted to evaluate translational relevance (ChiCTR2400082676). RESULTS: During acute stress, such as exercise or β-adrenergic stimulation, glutaminolysis was rapidly mobilized to supply mitochondrial glutathione, preserving mitochondrial redox homeostasis and sustaining cardiac contractile reserve. Mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase exhibited marked impairments in both contractile reserve and exercise capacity, accompanied by a failure to elevate mitochondrial glutathione and consequent mitochondrial oxidative stress. Chronic exercise training upregulated cardiac glutaminase expression and expanded the mitochondrial glutathione pool, linking this adaptive mechanism to training-induced improvements in cardiac reserve. In humans, acute oral glutamine supplementation enhanced cardiac reserve, as assessed by exercise stress echocardiography, in a placebo-controlled crossover design. CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a novel metabolic paradigm in which glutaminolysis functions as a dynamic pathway supporting mitochondrial health and cardiac resilience, and highlight glutamine supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance cardiac reserve.

recs.title: BAHCC1 Drives Smooth Muscle Plasticity and Neointima via Epigenetic Repression.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic plasticity drives neointimal hyperplasia (IH) and contributes to atherosclerosis. Epigenetic mechanisms have been implicated in SMC plasticity, but the roles of epigenetic reader proteins are poorly understood. BAHCC1 (bromo adjacent homology domain coiled-coil 1) is a newly identified reader of the gene-repression histone mark histone-3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3). Its role in vascular remodeling is unknown. METHODS: We investigated BAHCC1 in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and in rat and mouse arterial injury models using BAHCC1 silencing, SMC-specific deletion, and an H3K27me3-binding-deficient knock-in mutation. Mechanistic studies in human aortic SMCs integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling, protein-interaction assays, and single-guide RNA-dCas9-based epigenetic editing. RESULTS: BAHCC1 was upregulated in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and rat arteries with IH. While BAHCC1 silenc ing reduced IH in balloon-injured rat arteries, SMC-specific BAHCC1 deletion and the H3K27me3-binding-deficient mutation (BAHCC1Y2537A) attenuated IH in wire-injured mouse arteries. In human SMCs, mitogen induced BAHCC1 expression through nuclear factor Y subunit-α, promoting BAHCC1-dependent dedifferentiation. Integrated transcriptomics and epigenomics identified LMO7 (LIM domain only 7), an IH suppressor, as a key BAHCC1-repressed target. BAHCC1 occupancy at LMO7 required BAHCC1-H3K27me3 interaction, and LMO7-targeted H3K27me3 enrichment through epigenetic editing repressed its expression in a BAHCC1-dependent manner. Furthermore, BAHCC1 associated with SAP30 and RBBP4/7 to form a corepressor complex. Functionally, LMO7 silencing reversed the effects of BAHCC1 knockdown on human SMC phenotype and exacerbated IH in BAHCC1Y2537A mice. Human genetic analyses further identified BAHCC1 variants associated with cardiovascular phenotypes and BAHCC1 expression. CONCLUSIONS: BAHCC1 is a previously unrecognized epigenetic driver of vascular remodeling. By reading H3K27me3 and recruiting corepressors to repress gene expression, BAHCC1 promotes pathological SMC phenotypic transition and IH, highlighting the BAHCC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target for IH-associated vascular disease.

recs.title: Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Endovascular Reperfusion in Patients Without Intravenous Thrombolysis: A Subgroup Analysis of the PEARL Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke who undergo endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis, the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase (IAA) after successful endovascular reperfusion remain uncertain. METHODS: This was a prespecified subgroup analysis of the PEARL (Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Endovascular Reperfusion in Acute Stroke) randomized clinical trial conducted at 28 centers in China, focusing on patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis. Patients were stratified by treatment assignment: IAA treatment versus standard treatment (control). The primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving excellent functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1 at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, any intracranial hemorrhage within 36 hours, and 90-day all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Among 324 patients originally randomized in the PEARL trial, 189 underwent endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis and were included in this analysis. Of the 189 patients, 95 were assigned to the IAA treatment group and 94 to the standard treatment group. Excellent functional outcome at 90 days was significantly higher in the IAA treatment group compared with the standard treatment group (43.2% [41/95] versus 22.6% [21/93]; adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 1.86; 95% CI, 1.19-2.91; P=0.007). The absolute risk reduction was 20.6% (95% CI, 7.0%-33.1%). Results were consistent in per-protocol sensitivity analyses (P=0.002). No significant differences were observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aRR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.28-3.13; P=0.908), any intracranial hemorrhage (aRR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.68-1.60; P=0.843), or 90-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.49-2.04; P>0.99). CONCLUSIONS: In patients who did not receive prior intravenous thrombolysis, adjunctive IAA after successful endovascular thrombectomy was associated with a higher likelihood of excellent functional outcome at 90 days, without an apparent increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or mortality. REGISTRATION: URL: clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT05856851.

recs.title: Systemic Inflammation and Adverse Heart Failure Outcomes: Insights From the Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between systemic inflammation (SI) and outcomes among patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between SI and clinical and economic outcomes among individuals with HFpEF/HFmrEF. METHODS: We identified Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) testing from 2008 to 2022. We classified Veterans as with SI (hsCRP 2-10 mg/L) and without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L). The primary outcome was the 3-component major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) outcome of death, HF hospitalization, and HF-related emergency department encounters. Additional outcomes included acute care utilization and costs. We evaluated the adjusted associations between SI and clinical outcomes, acute care utilization, and costs via Cox regression, negative binomial regression, and gamma regression, respectively. RESULTS: We identified 49,986 Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient hsCRP levels. We compared 8,696 (17.4%) Veterans without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L) and 25,352 (50.7%) Veterans with SI (hsCRP ≥2 mg/L and ≤10 mg/L Over a median follow-up of 3.4 years (IQR: 1.8-5.8), MACE incidence was 15.1/100 patient-years (95% CI: 14.9-15.4) among those with SI vs 11.8/100 patient-years (95% CI: 11.4-12.1) among those without SI (P < 0.001). After adjustment, SI was associated with increased MACE (HR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.24-1.33). SI was also associated with increased all-cause hospitalizations (incidence rate ratio: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.137-1.246) and $9,112 (95% CI: $6,135-$12,089) in additional per-patient costs over 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: Among Veterans with HFmrEF/HFpEF, SI is associated with increased adverse clinical outcomes and higher costs.

recs.title: Vascular Brain Injury in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at higher risk of vascular brain lesions. Whether AF and HF synergistically amplify this risk is unclear. In this study, we explored the association of HF and AF and their interaction with the prevalence of MRI-detected vascular brain lesions. METHODS: We analysed 2,712 participants from the Swiss-AF study who underwent standardized brain-MRI and categorised them based on their AF diagnosis and history of HF. In the brain-MRI, we assessed large non-cortical and cortical infarcts (LNCCI), small non-cortical infarcts (SNCI) and white matter hyperintensities (WMH). Logistic regression models were used to analyse associations between AF, HF and their interaction with vascular brain lesions, adjusting for pre-selected covariates. RESULTS: Mean age was 73 years and 30.8% were female. The prevalence of ischemic brain infarcts and WMH increased across groups defined by AF and HF status (brain infarcts: AF-/HF- 22.8%, AF-/HF+ 30.2%, AF+/HF- 34.6%, AF+/HF+ 44.6%; WMH: AF-/HF- 43.2% AF-/HF+ 49.7%, AF+/HF- 50.4%, AF+/HF+ 65.6%). No significant interaction between AF and HF was observed for any brain lesion subtype. Both AF and HF (OR, 95% CI, p-value) were independently associated with brain infarcts (AF: 1.78, 1.48-2.16, p<0.001; HF: 1.32, 1.06-1.64, p<0.001) and WMH (AF: 1.71, 1.44-2.03, p<0.001; HF: 1.45, 1.17-1.80, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: AF and HF are independently associated with a higher prevalence of ischemic brain lesions, with the greatest burden observed in patients with both conditions. No interaction was found between AF and HF with regards to vascular brain lesions.

Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease. METHODS: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing. FINDINGS: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease. FUNDING: Agios Pharmaceuticals.

Association Between Cardiologist Ambulatory Workload and Evidence-Based Therapy for Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Most eligible patients are not prescribed guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF). Increased time pressures for providers in the ambulatory setting may contribute to these shortfalls. We assessed the association between cardiologist ambulatory workload and guideline-directed medical therapy prescription for patients with heart failure with reduced EF. METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study of patients with heart failure with reduced EF (EF ≤40%) seen by a cardiologist from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, using deidentified administrative and electronic health record data from Optum Labs Data Warehouse, which includes data from multiple health systems across the United States. The primary exposure was ambulatory workload, measured as the average number of visits per day, categorized into quartiles. The primary outcome was "comprehensive quadruple therapy," defined as prescription for all 4 guideline-directed medical therapies: β-blocker; angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor; mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor. Analyses were conducted using generalized estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and clinical variables. RESULTS: Overall, 40 173 patients were seen by 881 cardiologists (median ambulatory workload, 9.1 patients per day; interquartile range=5.1-13.0). The percentage of patients prescribed comprehensive quadruple therapy was higher among patients in lower quartiles (quartile 1: 14%; quartile 2: 9.7%; quartile 3: 8.9%; quartile 4: 7.4%; P<0.001). In adjusted analysis, there was a graded association between lower workload quartile and higher odds of comprehensive quadruple therapy, compared with the highest quartile (odds ratio [95% CI], P value=quartile 1: 1.35 [1.09-1.66], 0.008; quartile 2: 1.20 [1.00-1.43], 0.050; quartile 3: 1.11 [0.93-1.32], 0.28; quartile 4 [reference]). CONCLUSIONS: Seeing a cardiologist with lower ambulatory workload was associated with increased prescribing of guideline-recommended, life-saving therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced EF. Current models that incentivize more visits per day may negatively impact care in the ambulatory setting.

recs.title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

recs.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL. METHODS: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria. RESULTS: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups. CONCLUSIONS: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

recs.title: Identification of a Novel EBF1-Expressing Disease-Associated Arterial Subpopulation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a debilitating disease with a poor prognosis. However, only a limited number of palliative interventions are currently available. To address this unmet need, it is essential to understand the molecular causes of PAH by identifying unique disease-associated populations and their key molecular regulators during disease progression. METHODS: We constructed a single-cell multiome data set at 4 distinct time points during the pathogenesis of pulmonary hypertension (PH) using endothelial cells isolated from the Sugen5416/hypoxia rat model. We assessed the conservation of novel disease-associated endothelial cells by reanalyzing previously reported single-cell RNA sequencing data from human patients with PAH. We validated the functional importance of EBF1 (early B-cell factor 1) in PAH by performing in silico simulations and an in vivo knockdown mediated by a pulmonary endothelium-targeting associated virus. RESULTS: We found that PH progression gradually altered the transcriptional and epigenetic landscape of the pulmonary endothelium in a stage-specific manner, leading to the emergence of a novel disease-associated arterial endothelial population expressing EBF1. A similar endothelial subset was present in human patients with PAH. Immunofluorescence revealed that EBF1 expression was elevated in both human and rat lungs during PH progression. In silico simulations suggested that EBF1 is required for the pathogenic state, and the associated virus-mediated in vivo knockdown of Ebf1 ameliorated the pathological hallmarks of PH, including right ventricular systolic pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy, when delivered either before the onset of PH or after its establishment. CONCLUSIONS: We identified EBF1 as a key transcriptional regulator of a novel disease-associated population in both humans and rats. We further demonstrated that inhibiting EBF1 within the pulmonary endothelium ameliorates the pathological features of PH, suggesting that EBF1 and its transcriptional targets represent a novel and promising therapeutic avenue for PAH.

recs.title: Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
recs.abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women's cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women's cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.

Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026. STUDY SELECTION: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin). RESULTS: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study.
recs.abstract: AIMS: In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF. METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts). CONCLUSION: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity as Multicellular Network Failure: Cardiac Niche Reprogramming and Pathological Cell-Cell Communication.
recs.abstract: Anthracyclines are essential anticancer agents, yet a cardiomyocyte-centered model incompletely explains why cardiac injury can be delayed, progressive, and poorly captured by resting ejection fraction. We frame anthracycline cardiotoxicity as a multicellular network failure within the cardiac niche: the spatially organized interactions among cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, extracellular matrix, and circulating signals. Cardiomyocyte stress initiates injury, whereas pathological communication may propagate it. We distinguish a fibroblast-CD8+ T-cell adhesion circuit, supported by loss-of-function evidence in mice and correlative human data, from an emerging therapy-conditioned tumor-heart extracellular vesicle axis supported mainly by breast cancer models. These pathways may converge on fibrotic stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, and electrical uncoupling; however, direct cross-circuit interaction and drug-independent sufficiency remain unproven. We integrate established clinical risk modifiers with this framework, specify causal criteria, and propose spatial multiomics, living myocardial slices, tumor-bearing systems, and longitudinal phenotyping to test circuit persistence. This evidence-calibrated model shifts the goal from cataloging cell-intrinsic pathways to identifying mechanism-resolved biomarkers and therapeutically targetable communication nodes while preserving antitumor efficacy.
