Impact of surgical timing in left-sided infective endocarditis with persistently positive blood cultures.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Guidelines define persistent infection in infective endocarditis (IE) as positive blood cultures after 7 days of adequate antibiotic therapy. However, persistently positive blood cultures (PPBC) at 48 to 72 hours are already associated with a worse prognosis. We aimed to assess the clinical profile, temporal trends, and impact of surgical timing on outcomes in patients with left-sided IE and PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 3 Spanish tertiary centers (1998-2024). We compared patients with PPBC with those with blood culture clearance and assessed the effect of surgical timing using a time-dependent Cox model, inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, and a day-7 landmark analysis to minimize immortal time bias and confounding by indication. RESULTS: Among 1265 patients with positive baseline cultures, 283 (22.4%) had PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. These patients exhibited a more severe clinical and microbiological profile and higher in-hospital mortality (36.0% vs 22.3%; P < .001). In the day-7 landmark analysis, surgery within the first 7 days was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (HR, 0.53; 95%CI, 0.30-0.95), with consistent trends across the time-dependent Cox and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting models. CONCLUSIONS: PPBC at 48 to 72 hours identifies a high-risk subgroup of patients with left-sided IE. In these patients, early surgery within the first 7 days was associated with a potential survival benefit in adjusted models, supporting earlier reassessment of infection control to optimize surgical timing.

recs.title: How Much Is Too Much?
Neuropsychological and Quality-of-Life Outcomes After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage often have long-term neuropsychological disturbances. This study aims to characterize depressive symptoms, quality of life, and personality changes in a large cohort of survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included patients with a history of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from the Brain Aneurysm Foundation patient registry. Patients completed the Beck Depression Inventory-II and the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life scale, and family members completed the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Multiple linear regression was used to identify symptoms associated with reduced work productivity. Wilcoxon and chi-square tests were used to identify variables associated with severity of depressive symptoms and personality changes. RESULTS: A total of 318 patients were included, with 242 completing the Beck Depression Inventory-II and Stroke-Specific Quality of Life, and 112 family members completing the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Moderate depressive symptoms were reported by 18% of patients, and severe symptoms were reported by 11%. Impairments in thinking, social roles, language, and energy were independently associated with reduced work productivity. Acquired personality disturbances were observed in 72% of patients for executive function, 44% for social behavior, 49% for hypomotivation, 50% for irascibility, and 72% for distress. Ruptured aneurysms in the anterior cerebral and anterior communicating artery were associated with a trend toward a higher prevalence of moderate to severe depressive symptoms and executive personality changes. CONCLUSIONS: Depressive symptoms and personality changes are common after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, affecting work productivity. Recognizing challenges in thinking, social interactions, language, and vulnerability to pressure may help guide targeted interventions by families, employers, and health care providers.

recs.title: From Risk Trajectories to Surrogate Endpoints in Mild HCM.
Assessment of Persistent Postpartum Hypertension Following Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals with persistent postpartum hypertension (ppHTN) after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is an important strategy to mitigate associated long-term cardiovascular risks. Accordingly, we aimed to review the literature surrounding the assessment of ppHTN after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework. We developed and pilot-tested a data extraction tool to collect information on ppHTN assessment methods, including timing and setting, blood pressure (BP) thresholds used, and inclusion of patient preferences. Data were synthesized into tables and narrative summaries. Barriers and facilitators to BP assessment protocols, remote BP monitoring, and follow-up attendance were mapped using the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework. RESULTS: Of 14 593 records, 96 papers met inclusion criteria. BP measured in the hospital alone was most common (n=41), followed by the hospital/home combination (n=18), and the outpatient/home combination (n=9). Monitoring typically began within 0 to 7 days postpartum (n=28), ending at 1 to 6 weeks (n=20) or 6 to 12 months (n=20) postpartum. ppHTN was defined using elevated BP thresholds (n=28), most commonly ≥140/90 mm Hg (n=18), medication initiation (n=8), lack of BP normalization over time (n=4), or referral to a specialist (n=2). Only 7 studies assessed patient preferences. Facilitators to home BP assessment included the use of educational material, while barriers involved digital access limitations. CONCLUSIONS: ppHTN assessment methods varied in timing, setting, and BP thresholds. Findings underscore the need for standardized, patient-centered guidelines that account for BP assessment methods across settings.

recs.title: Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk. METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum. RESULTS: Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS (P=0.784). CONCLUSIONS: In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

recs.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Automated Optical Coherence Tomography Analysis for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Planning: From Plaque Analysis to Precision Lesion Preparation and Stent Optimization.
recs.abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains the cornerstone of revascularization in coronary artery disease. However, despite advances in stent technology, adverse outcomes related to suboptimal stent placement including under-expansion, malapposition, incomplete coverage, edge dissection, and neoatherosclerosis persist. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the highest resolution widely available intravascular imaging modality, allowing unparalleled visualization of stent-vessel interactions and plaque morphology. However, there are significant barriers to large-scale OCT adoption, including time-consuming manual interpretation and dependence on the operator, resulting in significant variability between analysts. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based automated OCT analysis promises to assist PCI by delivering rapid, reproducible, and standardized stent optimization, but current analysis systems lack important features to optimize stent placement. This review summarizes the principles of OCT in PCI, the evidence for OCT-guided optimization, and recent advances in AI-driven automated OCT analysis. We discuss plaque analysis and classification, highlighting how AI-driven automated OCT analysis can identify fibrous, lipid-rich, and calcified lesions and guide tailored lesion preparation using balloons, specialty balloons, drug-coated balloons, intravascular lithotripsy, and atherectomy. We outline emerging AI-enabled workflows for fully automated PCI optimization, evaluate clinical outcomes, interpretability, and workflow integration. Finally, we explore future directions including AI imaging-physiology fusion, multiomics integration, and robotics. If successful, automated AI-empowered OCT analysis could become a central imaging platform for precision PCI, enabling tailored lesion preparation, optimal stent deployment, and improved clinical outcomes in coronary artery disease management.

recs.title: Impact of obesity on clinical outcomes and the treatment effect of catheter ablation in atrial fibrillation: insights from CABANA.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Obesity and atrial fibrillation (AF) are global epidemics, often co-existing and compounding cardiovascular risk. While catheter ablation has emerged as an effective strategy for rhythm control in symptomatic AF, it remains unclear whether obesity modifies its benefit. This post hoc analysis of the CABANA trial investigates the influence of baseline obesity on clinical outcomes after catheter ablation vs. drug therapy in AF patients. METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 2170 CABANA participants with available body mass index (BMI) were included. Obesity was defined by BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, and Class II obesity by BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Adverse outcomes, AF recurrence, and functional status were analysed using Cox, mixed-effects, and generalized estimating equation models, assessing treatment-by-obesity interactions. Obese patients exhibited higher comorbidity burden, worse baseline functional status, and more persistent AF compared to non-obese counterparts. Higher BMI was associated with increased cardiovascular hospitalization and a higher New York Heart Association functional class. Catheter ablation significantly reduced the risk of AF recurrence and improved symptom burden and functional capacity, irrespective of obesity status. No significant interaction was found between BMI and treatment effect on the primary composite endpoint of cardiovascular hospitalization or all-cause mortality. However, patients with Class II obesity or higher had worse absolute outcomes despite similar relative benefits from ablation. CONCLUSION: While obesity is associated with worse baseline status and outcomes, it was not shown to significantly alter the relative effectiveness of AF ablation compared to drug therapy. These findings support a multifaceted approach integrating rhythm control with upstream interventions targeting obesity-related atrial remodelling and comorbidity management.

recs.title: Vascular Function and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Adults Who Use Nicotine Vapes.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The rising use of nicotine vapes among young adults who have never smoked combustible tobacco raises concerns regarding potential early cardiovascular and respiratory effects in an otherwise low-risk population. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether regular daily nicotine vape use is associated with altered vascular function and cardiorespiratory fitness in young adults without established cardiovascular risk factors. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a cross-sectional, single-center, laboratory-based physiological assessment study conducted between July 2023 and April 2025 among young adults without known cardiovascular disease or major risk factors. Based on self-report and verification of smoking status, participants were stratified into 3 groups: adults who exclusively used nicotine vapes, adults who used combustible cigarettes, and tobacco- and nicotine vape-naive individuals. Data analysis was performed from September 2023 to April 2025. EXPOSURE: Regular daily use of nicotine vapes or combustible cigarettes. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes included vascular function, assessed by flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and carotid artery reactivity (CAR), and cardiorespiratory fitness, assessed through ventilatory, metabolic, and cardiac responses during maximal cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Secondary measures included spirometry results and physical activity. RESULTS: Fifty-eight young adults (mean [SD] age, 26 [7] years; 30 [52%] female) were included, among whom 17 exclusively used nicotine vapes, 19 used combustible cigarettes, and 22 were tobacco and nicotine vape naive. Lung function and physical activity levels did not differ significantly across groups. FMD and CAR were lower both in adults who used nicotine vapes (mean [SD] FMD, 5.5% [3.4%]; mean [SD] CAR, 0.6% [5.3%]) and in adults who used combustible cigarettes (mean [SD] FMD, 4.4% [2.9%]; mean [SD] CAR, -1.4% [5.3%]) compared with tobacco- and nicotine vape-naive individuals (mean [SD] FMD, 8.3% [3.4%]; mean [SD] CAR, 4.7% [3.2%]). Peak oxygen uptake was lower in adults who used nicotine vapes compared with tobacco- and nicotine vape-naive individuals but did not differ significantly between combustible cigarette and naive groups; minute ventilation and cardiac output were lower in both nicotine use groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Regular daily nicotine vape use in young adults who have never smoked combustible tobacco was associated with lower vascular function and cardiorespiratory fitness. These findings highlight the need for longitudinal studies to determine long-term clinical implications.

recs.title: Safety and Outcomes of Transvenous Lead Extraction of Advisory ePTFE-Coated Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Leads: A Multicenter Experience With RELIANCE G.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE)-coated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are associated with progressive coil calcification and rising shock impedance, prompting a recent safety advisory. However, data regarding the safety and efficacy of transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for these chronic leads remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and procedural outcomes of TLE in patients with advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads. METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study at 13 centers of patients undergoing TLE of ePTFE-coated ICD leads. Primary endpoints included procedural success, complications, and short-term mortality. Multivariable analyses identified predictors of outcomes. RESULTS: Among 423 patients undergoing extraction of advisory RELIANCE ICD leads (Boston Scientific), mean lead dwell time was 7.5 ± 5.3 years, and impedance-defined coil calcification was present in 15.1%. Laser sheaths were used in 63.8% of procedures and multiple extraction tools in 21.7%. Complete lead removal was achieved in 95.5%, clinical success in 98.8%, and extraction failed occurred in 1.2%. Major complications occurred in 0.9% of patients, with no procedural deaths. Calcified leads were associated with longer dwell times but not higher rates of major complications. Thirty-day mortality was 2.8%, primarily among patients undergoing extraction for infection. CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, TLE of advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads was associated with high procedural success and low major complication rates despite long lead dwell times. Outcomes were consistent with contemporary TLE experience and do not suggest increased procedural risk attributable to this lead model. The presence of impedance-defined coil calcification did not adversely affect procedural outcomes, supporting TLE at experienced centers when clinically indicated.

recs.title: Acute exacerbation of chronic chest pain in a middle-aged man.
Pulmonary Pressure Trajectories After Mitral TEER: Beyond Baseline Risk.
Not All Strokes Are Equal: Phenotype-Dependent Surgical Timing in Infective Endocarditis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: We evaluated postoperative neurologic and mortality outcomes by stroke-to-surgery timing and stroke phenotype in patients with left-sided infective endocarditis. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing surgery for infective endocarditis complicated by preoperative stroke between 2004 and 2024 at 2 institutions were stratified by stroke-to-surgery interval (<1 week, 1-4 weeks, 4-6 weeks). The primary outcome was a composite postoperative cerebrovascular event: new stroke, enlarging stroke, or hemorrhagic conversion. Secondary outcomes were operative death and major morbidity events. RESULTS: Among 2265 patients with left-sided infective endocarditis, 322 met inclusion criteria, of whom 122 (38%) underwent surgery within 1 week, 168 (52%) between 1 and 4 weeks, and 32 (10%) between 4 and 6 weeks. Operative death was similar across groups (P=0.09). Postoperative cerebrovascular events declined with time (<1 week, 21.3%; 1-4 weeks, 11.9%; 4-6 weeks, 9.4%; P=0.015). On multivariable analysis, longer stroke-to-surgery interval was associated with reduced odds of postoperative cerebrovascular events (odds ratio, 0.92/d [95% CI, 0.85-0.98]; P=0.015), driven by early events among patients with intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli. Among ischemic strokes, operative death was lowest with surgery within 1 week (5.8% versus 11.2% at 1-4 weeks; P=0.24). Interval embolization occurred in 10.6% of patients awaiting surgery, most commonly affecting the spleen and kidneys. CONCLUSIONS: Excess postoperative neurologic risk was concentrated within the first 7 to 10 days and driven by intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli; ischemic stroke showed no appreciable temporal association. Routine delay after ischemic stroke may not be necessary, while a short delay (≈7 days) for hemorrhagic and septic embolic subtypes may be reasonable when hemodynamically feasible.

recs.title: Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy Demonstrated by Coronary Angiography and Histopathological Correlates.
Pulmonary Artery Dissection Identified by Optical Coherence Tomography in Takayasu Arteritis.
Small Annulus: Follow-Up Marker Rather Than Treatment Selector?
Complementary Cardiohepatic Prognostic Value of Hepatic Steatosis in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis carries substantial cardiovascular risk, whereas cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome contributes to liver disease progression, highlighting the need for integrated cardiohepatic risk assessment. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate whether hepatic steatosis provides incremental prognostic value beyond CKM staging for cardiovascular and liver outcomes. METHODS: We included 313,970 UK Biobank participants with CKM stages 0 to 3. Hepatic steatosis was primarily assessed using the Fatty Liver Index, with the Hepatic Steatosis Index as an alternative measure and the Fibrosis-4 Index for liver fibrosis. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The secondary outcome was major adverse liver events (MALEs). RESULTS: During a median 15.7-year follow-up, 32,110 MACEs and 1,599 MALEs occurred. Hepatic steatosis and advanced CKM were independently associated with both outcomes, with coexistence conferring the highest risks (MACEs: HR: 2.33; 95% CI: 2.19-2.47; MALEs: HR: 5.09; 95% CI: 3.97-6.54, vs neither exposure). For MACEs, the association with hepatic steatosis was stronger in nonadvanced CKM (stages 0-2: HR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.48-1.55) than in stage 3 (HR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.97-1.23; Pinteraction < 0.001). For MALEs, hepatic steatosis mediated 41.1% of the association with CKM stage. The findings were consistent across alternative steatosis measures, whereas liver fibrosis showed no significant stage-dependent association with MACEs and a smaller mediation proportion for MALEs. Adding hepatic steatosis to CKM staging improved discrimination for both outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic steatosis provided complementary cardiovascular and liver prognostic value beyond CKM staging, supporting its integration for more comprehensive cardiohepatic risk stratification.

recs.title: Health Care Use and Outcomes in Heart Failure: Are There Lingering Impacts From the COVID-19 Pandemic?
CCR2-Dependent Myeloid Cell Recruitment Links Post-MI Heart Failure to Pulmonary Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) is a common complication of myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure (HF). Myeloid inflammation is a major hallmark of both the local cardiac and systemic post-MI response, with resident and recruited monocyte-derived macrophages orchestrating each step of the ensuing inflammatory cascade, from clearance of dead cardiomyocytes to scar tissue formation. Similarly, myeloid inflammation is a key feature of the PH lung, driving remodeling of small pulmonary vessels. We thus hypothesized that MI-induced systemic myeloid inflammation contributes directly to the development of PH-LHD. METHODS: We assessed expression of inflammatory adhesion molecules, as markers of vascular inflammatory activation and myeloid cell recruitment pathways, in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, PH-LHD, as well as in a PH-LHD rat model. We then induced MI and subsequent HF in 8- to 10-week-old female C57BL/6J mice via permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. HF mice were then treated with a CCR2 (C-C chemokine receptor 2) antagonist to block monocyte recruitment and the development of PH-LHD was assessed at 6 weeks post-MI by a combination of invasive hemodynamics, flow cytometry, echocardiography, and lung histology. RESULTS: Expression of key inflammatory adhesion molecules, including VCAM1 and SELE, was increased in PH-LHD lungs from humans and rats. Following early post-MI development of HF with reduced ejection fraction, mice exhibited increased numbers of circulating monocytes, lung monocytes, and lung interstitial macrophages, as well as PH-LHD by 6 weeks, characterized by right ventricular hypertrophy, elevated right ventricular pressures, and lung vascular remodeling of small-to-medium-sized pulmonary vessels. Administration of the selective CCR2 antagonist RS102895 from day 10 post-MI to reduce monocyte tissue recruitment attenuated lung vascular remodeling, right ventricular systolic and diastolic pressures, right ventricular hypertrophy, and lung adhesion molecule expression at 6 weeks, compared with vehicle-treated controls, without improving the underlying left-sided HF. CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a causal role for CCR2-dependent myeloid cell recruitment in the progression from MI-induced HF to secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

recs.title: Using rare coding variants in SLC5A2 to explore the impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on cardiorenal outcomes.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are agents originally developed as glucose-lowering drugs but now widely used to improve cardiorenal outcomes, including in patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease regardless of diabetes status. However, their exact mode of action remains unclear. Here, we investigated the association of loss-of-function (LoF) and other rare coding variants in the SLC5A2 gene, as a genetic model of altered SGLT2 function, with 13 cardiometabolic and renal traits and clinical outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 442 570 European ancestry participants from the UK Biobank with exome sequence and phenotype data were included. We applied SAIGE-GENE+ for gene-based and single-variant association tests in the full study population and in individuals with heart failure, renal failure, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). A total of 52 LoF variants in SLC5A2 were identified. Rare variants in SLC5A2 were associated with decreased uric acid (PCauchy = 4.98 × 10-13) and with increased haematocrit (PCauchy = 1.67 × 10-5), haemoglobin (PCauchy = 1.60 × 10-5), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (PCauchy = 9.88 × 10-4). One frameshift variant (rs267607067) was significantly associated with increased haemoglobin (β = 0.33 [95% CI 0.15-0.51]; P-value = 2.40 × 10-4) and another (rs768095044) with decreased uric acid (β = -0.31 [95% CI -0.49 to -0.13]; P-value = 4.22 × 10-4). In patients with T2D, the rare variants within SLC5A2 were also associated with a lower probability of having heart failure (PCauchy = 4.00 × 10-4). CONCLUSION: Rare genetic variants in SLC5A2 were associated with increased haemoglobin and decreased uric acid. These variants were also associated with a lower probability of heart failure among participants with T2D, providing tentative genetic support for a cardioprotective effect of SGLT2 inhibition.

recs.title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium: FRACTURE Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a promising option to modify calcium. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. METHODS: FRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed. RESULTS: A total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). CONCLUSIONS: The quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation. REGISTRATION: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240).

recs.title: Redefining Cardiometabolic Disease: Expert Consensus on the CardioVascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic (CVKLM) Multiorgan Staging.
recs.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases increasingly manifest as interconnected dysfunction across the heart, vasculature, kidneys, liver, and metabolic system. The global rise in obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes, together with therapies benefiting multiple organs, has reshaped the epidemiology and understanding of cardiometabolic disease, exposing the limitations of organ-specific or single-stage approaches. The cardioVascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CVKLM) framework is a multidimensional staging system in which cardiac, vascular, kidney, liver, and metabolic involvement are graded independently from absent to advanced. Analogous to tumour-node-metastasis staging, it provides a standardized language describing disease severity within each organ and its distribution across organs. Rather than replacing existing classifications, CVKLM integrates universal heart failure stages, validated vascular risk assessment, KDIGO chronic kidney disease stratification, contemporary metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and advanced liver disease criteria, and current definitions of diabetes and clinical obesity. Unlike hierarchical frameworks assigning a single overall stage, CVKLM preserves organ-specific information and records coexisting abnormalities across domains. Intended for clinical and research phenotyping and staging rather than as a validated global risk score, it may facilitate systematic recognition of concomitant organ disease, support existing organ-specific diagnostic, referral, and treatment pathways, and provide a standardized taxonomy for observational studies and clinical trials. The prognostic significance of CVKLM profiles, their incremental value beyond established risk tools, and their clinical utility remain to be established. By integrating these domains within a common architecture, CVKLM offers a pragmatic framework spanning the full spectrum of cardiometabolic disease, from preclinical involvement to advanced multiorgan failure.

recs.title: Precision medicine for pediatric cardiomyopathy: lessons from pediatric oncology.
Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs. OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs. METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety. RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type. CONCLUSION: These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.

recs.title: Reply: Trajectory-Based Myocardial Remodeling and MACE Risk in Phenotypically Mild HCM.
One-Lung Ventilation to Facilitate Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair Under Transesophageal Echocardiographic Imaging.
Extrinsic Left Main Coronary Compression Caused by Delayed Periaortic Hematoma After Aortic Valve Replacement.
Stroke Risk Prediction in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: Simplicity, Complexity, and the Modern Paradigm Shift.
Role for Factor XIa Inhibitors after an Acute Coronary Syndrome Event.
Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery. METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge. RESULTS: A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046). CONCLUSIONS: While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

recs.title: Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction (TVME) in the systemic circulation is increasingly being reported. However, its feasibility, effectiveness, and safety remain poorly defined. AIMS: We sought to investigate the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of TVME in the left heart and aortic arch. METHODS: Consecutive patients from 6 centres in the United States and Canada were included. Feasibility was defined as technically successful mass extraction without unplanned cardiac surgery or intraprocedural mortality. The effectiveness endpoint was feasibility with successful debulking of ≥70% mass volume. The primary safety endpoint was the 30-day composite of procedure-attributable mortality, major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke, all according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 definitions. Intraprocedural events were also reported. RESULTS: A total of 62 consecutive patients were evaluated. Feasibility was reached in 85.5% of patients and effectiveness in 77.4% of patients - except for 11.3% with suboptimal debulking, 3.2% with access-related case abortion, and 8.1% with case cancellation where no mass was found intraprocedurally. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 14.5% of patients, with a procedure-attributable mortality rate of 3.2%. VARC-3 major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, ACS, and stroke occurred in 3.2%, 8.1%, 3.2%, 3.2%, and 6.5% of patients, respectively. Intraprocedural events included hypoxia (6.5%), hypotension (9.7%), embolism (3.2%), air embolism (1.6%), and increased mitral regurgitation (6.5%). CONCLUSIONS: TVME in left-sided and aortic arch masses is feasible and demonstrates reasonable effectiveness. However, the considerable rate of safety-related events highlights the need for better case selection and procedural refinement, such as optimal embolic protection.

recs.title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events. METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model. RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

recs.title: Temporal Trends and Autopsy Correlates of Duty-Related Cardiac Death in Firefighters.
Day-Night Patterns of Wearable-Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Left Atrial Remodeling in Atrial Fibrillation-Naïve Individuals.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-derived electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) age is conventionally treated as a static marker. Its diurnal dynamics and structural correlates in individuals without atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unknown. OBJECTIVE: To characterize diurnal AI-ECG age patterns, their reproducibility, and associations with left atrial (LA) remodeling. METHODS: We analyzed continuous wearable ECGs from two prospective registries (NCT05119725, NCT05355948). In 499 AF-naïve participants with ≥48-hour recordings, AI-ECG age was estimated every 10 minutes. Unsupervised clustering identified day-night trajectories, summarized by day-night difference (ΔAge) into Restorative (>0.6 years) or Disrupted (≤0.6 years) phenotypes. Reproducibility was evaluated across sequential periods. Age- and sex-adjusted associations of binary and continuous ΔAge with LA volume index (LAVI) were pooled in a cross-sectional echocardiographic substudy (n=122). RESULTS: Three trajectories emerged in both registries. Restorative prevalence was 47.6%-50.2%. Agreement between two consecutive 48-hour periods was 75.8% (κ = 0.516; 95% CI, 0.395-0.631); 6- to 8-day intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.51-0.54. The Disrupted phenotype was associated with higher LAVI (pooled mean difference, 5.54 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.11-9.98; P = .014) and greater odds of LA enlargement (LAVI ≥40 mL/m2; pooled odds ratio, 3.68; 95% CI, 1.45-9.29; P = .006). Per 1-SD higher ΔAge, LAVI was lower (β, -2.89 mL/m2; P = .007) and LA enlargement less likely (odds ratio, 0.53; P = .004). CONCLUSION: Wearable-derived AI-ECG age exhibits a reproducible day-night pattern. A Disrupted phenotype is associated with adverse LA remodeling. Because reproducibility remains insufficient for individual-level classification, prospective outcome-based validation is warranted.

recs.title: Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium. OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia. RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35). CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

recs.title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group. METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia. RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout. CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

recs.title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry. METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria. RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis. CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

Beyond tetramer stability: wild-type ATTR-CM as a disease of the ageing myocardium.
The Duke Clinically Linked Electrocardiogram and Arrhythmia Repository.
recs.abstract: Artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram (ECG) algorithms are becoming increasingly powerful tools in the clinical world, allowing for earlier and subclinical detection of ubiquitous and harmful pathologies. However, the strength of these algorithms is directly informed by the strength of the data sets on which they are trained, and there is a growing need for large-scale, diverse, publicly available ECG repositories. The Duke Clinically Linked ECG and Arrhythmia Repository is a large-scale ECG database containing over 5 million clinically acquired ECGs linked to longitudinal clinical data. Its strengths-including demographic diversity, large sample size, linked clinical databases, breadth of represented conditions, access to linked procedure codes, various options for data export, and ease in creating targeted subcohorts-position it as a significant tool in the artificial intelligence-ECG research landscape. This Methods paper outlines the demographics and structure of this database and explores promising research applications of this resource.

recs.title: Pulmonary Hypertension and Its Association With Cardiac Transplant Outcomes: Does Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure Matter?
Correction to: Reevaluating the Use of Race/Ethnicity in the MESA Risk Score.
PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR). METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed. RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087). CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

recs.title: A Novel Method for Assessing Left Bundle Branch Capture Using the Bidirectional Conduction Time Difference Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Coronary Sinus Leads.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an established conduction system pacing strategy; however, confirming left bundle branch (LBB) capture remains challenging. OBJECTIVE: We propose a novel method for LBB capture confirmation based on the bidirectional conduction time difference between the LBBAP and coronary sinus (CS) leads. METHODS: This observational study included 60 patients undergoing de novo left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy. LBB capture was defined by (1) paced QRS transition, (2) LBB potential with current of injury, or (3) ΔV6 R-wave peak time ≥10 ms. LBBAP-to-CS and CS-to-LBBAP conduction times were measured. ΔLBB-CS ([CS-to-LBBAP] - [LBBAP-to-CS]) was compared between nonselective LBB pacing (NS-LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP). RESULTS: Among 60 patients (74.7±10.4 years; 42 men), 25 had left bundle branch block and 17 had non-specific intraventricular conduction delay. LBB capture was confirmed in 45 patients (75.0%). LBBAP-to-CS was 114.3±28.0 ms during NS-LBBP (n=43) and 134.2±19.0 ms during LVSP (n=29), whereas CS-to-LBBAP was 143.4±28.5 ms (n=60). ΔLBB-CS was greater during NS-LBBP than LVSP (27.5±9.9 vs. 7.9±7.4 ms, P<0.01). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a 21.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture (74.4% sensitivity; 100% specificity; area under curve [AUC] 0.95). In patients with baseline LBBB (n=25), a 20.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture yielded 92.9% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and an AUC of 0.99. CONCLUSION: ΔLBB-CS ≥ 21.5ms may serve as a novel adjunctive marker of LBB capture during LOT-CRT, with greater diagnostic accuracy at a 20.5 ms cutoff in patients with baseline LBBB.

recs.title: Role of Plasma Proteins in the Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Disease Events: Results From Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Cohorts.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Socioeconomic status (SES) is strongly associated with cardiovascular disease burden and risk. Plasma proteins may elucidate a biological mechanism through which low SES increases the risk of cardiovascular disease. METHODS: Participants from the following 3 cohorts were included: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (n=2139), Jackson Heart Study (n=967), and Women's Health Initiative (n=1104). SES was approximated using a cumulative score (range 0-3) across education, income, and employment status. A meta-analysis of Cox proportional hazards ratios was used to assess the association between SES and incident events for coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke. Linear regression was used within each cohort to determine associations between SES and Olink proteins (n=1270 proteins) and the results were meta-analyzed across cohorts. Regression-based mediation analysis was used to determine whether the identified proteins were statistical mediators of the association of SES and incident events. RESULTS: Higher SES scores were associated with a lower risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.87]) and stroke (HR, 0.81 [95% CI, 0.66-1.00]). After correcting for multiple testing (P<3.937×10-5), 233 proteins were associated with SES in the meta-analysis. Of these 233 proteins, 21 had a significant indirect effect on SES and CHD. Because the SES-stroke association was not statistically significant, proteins were not tested as mediators. CONCLUSIONS: Our analysis of multiple cohorts identified evidence of different proteomic pathways associated with SES and cardiovascular disease. This work suggests that exogenous social factors (eg, SES) may influence cardiovascular disease via proteomic profiles.

Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

recs.title: Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy. RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016). CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

recs.title: Undiagnosed Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy Hidden in Explanted Hearts: Insights from a Single Tertiary Center.
Great debate: a dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome.
recs.abstract: Suspected myocardial infarction in patients with acute chest pain at rest is one of the most common diagnostic categories leading to emergency hospital admission and emergency department overcrowding worldwide. Efforts are being made to improve the efficiency of currently used triage and diagnostic work-up strategies. Despite major advances in recent years with the use of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, challenges still exist regarding how to accurately and rapidly rule out or rule in myocardial infarction, as current strategies are relatively slow due to the need for serial troponin measurements. The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommend a 0 h/1 h or a 0 h/2 h high-sensitivity troponin diagnostic algorithm, instead of the previously suggested 0 h/3 h diagnostic protocol, to reduce the time required to discharge patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction. The ESC endorsed algorithms are not without difficulty, and alternative ways of improving triaging have been proposed, particularly a dual biomarker rule-out strategy involving the combined measurement of copeptin and troponin. Supporters of the dual biomarker strategy argue that a timely optimized algorithm can potentially allow the safe rule-out of myocardial infarction earlier than currently used strategies. In the present Great Debate article, two expert teams discuss the 'pros' and 'cons' of implementing single vs dual biomarker strategies for the rule-in and rule-out of myocardial infarction, under the moot topic 'A dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome'. They address in detail many of the controversial issues currently affecting everyday clinical practice and provide insightful comments on how to best triage patients presenting with suspected acute myocardial infarction.

recs.title: Specific effects of Pulsed Field Ablation on the cardiac tissue, the nervous system and the conduction system in experimental and clinical studies.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel ablation modality for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias and has rapidly reshaped contemporary electrophysiology practice. This article provides a comprehensive analysis on the mechanisms underlying the specific effects of PFA on myocardial, neural tissue structures, and the cardiac conduction system, integrating biophysical principles with preclinical and clinical evidence relevant to contemporary electrophysiology practice. METHODS AND RESULTS: This document provides an exhaustive mechanistic explanation for the preferential effects of PFA on myocardium and the limits of the 'tissue-selectivity' concept. The complex interplay between cellular and tissue-level biophysics, biological responses, and tissue regenerative capacity that determines differential susceptibility to electroporation across tissues is analysed. Distinct patterns of lesion formation and maturation following PFA are also reviewed, highlighting the temporal and histopathological differences compared with radiofrequency ablation. Additionally, lesion formation in heterogeneous substrates is analysed, including fibrotic and adipose-rich myocardium, where local electric field distribution critically influences lesion durability. CONCLUSION: The article further examines the interaction between pulsed electric fields and neural tissue, with emphasis on the phrenic nerve and intrinsic cardiac autonomic nervous system. While nerve stimulation and transient reversible conduction disturbances produced by reversible electroporation can occur during ablation, permanent neural injury appears extremely rare in current clinical experience. Finally, this manuscript examines current understanding regarding the specific effects of PFA on the cardiac conduction system, which according to the limited available evidence appear strongly dependent on electric field dose and anatomical proximity.

recs.title: Prognosis of Native T1 Mapping in TTR Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: Beaten to the Finish Line by Extracellular Volume.
Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included. EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores. RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

recs.title: Family Screening and Disease Predictors in Gene-Elusive Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Family screening is recommended in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), but risk stratification of relatives of probands without pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (gene-elusive) remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to define the incidence, prognosis, and predictors of disease development in first-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands. METHODS: First-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands from 4 international referral centers who underwent baseline electrocardiography and echocardiography were included. The primary outcome was the development of the disease, defined as DCM or isolated left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction (LV ejection fraction: <50%). Major adverse cardiac events were exploratory secondary outcomes. Age-adjusted Cox models with family-clustered robust standard errors were used to identify disease predictors. RESULTS: Among 292 relatives (median age: 36 years, 48% male), 14 (5%) were affected at baseline. During a median follow-up of 52 months, 21 additional relatives developed disease, corresponding to an incidence rate of 17 per 1,000 person-years. Familial DCM (HR: 4.24; 95% CI: 1.38-13.1; P = 0.012), QRS duration >120 ms (HR: 7.24; 95% CI: 2.25-23.3; P < 0.001), lower LV ejection fraction (HR: 3.73; 95% CI: 2.46-5.65; P < 0.001), and LV dilatation (HR: 6.19; 95% CI: 2.27-16.9; P < 0.001) were predictors of disease development. Age at diagnosis in probands significantly correlated with age at onset in relatives (r = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.55-0.92; P < 0.001). Major adverse cardiac events occurred in 9 patients (4%). CONCLUSIONS: First-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands have a relatively low but non-negligible risk of disease development. Familial clustering, electrocardiographic or echocardiographic abnormalities, and age of disease expression in the proband may help tailor surveillance intensity.

recs.title: Disparities in Editorial Leadership of Highly Cited Cardiology Journals by Gender and Country Income Classification.
Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms. METHODS: BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device. RESULTS: Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

recs.title: AI algorithms and external validation: promises, pitfalls, and a practical blueprint.
recs.abstract: External validation involving the testing of a frozen AI model on independent data from other sites, populations, time periods, or devices provides the clearest estimate of intended-use setting performance when those external data are deployment-representative of the expected population, measurement processes, and clinical workflow. It yields realistic estimates of discrimination and calibration, exposes shortcut learning and distribution shift, quantifies clinical utility through decision-analytic measures, and reveals subgroup disparities requiring mitigation. Yet common pitfalls undermine credibility: quasi-external splits with hidden relatedness; spectrum and prevalence mismatch; site, workflow, and hardware effects; label noise and reference-standard drift; analytic flexibility and selective reporting; small, underpowered samples; reliance only on the area under the curve; unreported threshold tuning; and leakage. A practical blueprint emphasizes pre-registration; representative, multi-site cohorts spanning geography, time, and acquisition; prevention of patient and temporal overlap; comprehensive evaluation of discrimination, calibration (including calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and calibration plots), and net benefit with confidence intervals; pre-specified subgroup and fairness audits; transparent labelling procedures and uncertainty analyses; principled sample-size calculations; and minimal, well-documented model updating (recalibration before revision). Finally, external validation should connect to post-deployment governance via drift detection, performance triggers, and change-control plans, complemented by site-specific local evaluation to ensure safety and reliability across diverse clinical environments. When executed to these standards, external validation transforms promising prototypes into dependable clinical tools, clarifying where a model performs, where it fails, and what adaptations are necessary for safe, equitable, and sustainable use. This framework links statistical evaluation to clinical use, model updating, and post-deployment monitoring.

Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics. RESULTS: Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

The perspective of combining pulsed field ablation and left atrial appendage closure.
recs.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) are increasingly discussed as complementary strategies in atrial fibrillation (AF) care, addressing rhythm control and long-term thromboembolic risk. The rationale is attractive, but the current evidence base is uneven. Randomized evidence for LAAC around AF ablation is strongest for thermal-ablation-era workflows, particularly the OPTION trial, which showed lower non-procedure-related major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding with LAAC than with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and non-inferiority for death, stroke, or systemic embolism. Dedicated PFA-specific evidence remains limited to feasibility studies and early observational experience, and no trial has demonstrated that combined ablation-LAAC procedures are clinically superior when the ablation component is performed with PFA rather than radiofrequency or cryoballoon ablation. In parallel, OAC-withdrawal trials after apparently successful ablation, including OCEAN and ALONE-AF, have reported low thromboembolic event rates in selected lower-risk populations, whereas CLOSURE-AF cautions against simple extrapolation of LAAC benefit to older, frailer patients at high stroke and bleeding risk. This review therefore positions combined PFA-LAAC as a potential option for carefully selected patients rather than an established routine strategy. We summarize procedural workflow, patient selection, trial populations, device-platform considerations, reimbursement and organizational issues, and the main uncertainties that should guide future prospective studies.
