Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. METHODS: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). FINDINGS: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156). INTERPRETATION: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

recs.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
recs.abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

Macrophage-derived TNF-α promotes vascular inflammation and cell crosstalk in human atherosclerotic plaques via TNFRSF1A.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by complex cellular crosstalk within plaques. How a key inflammatory pathway orchestrates multicellular vascular injury and whether this is conserved across vascular beds remains incompletely understood. METHODS: Carotid and coronary plaques were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. Immunofluorescence validated cell localization and TNF-TNFRSF1A signaling, and CellChat analyzed intercellular communication. THP-1 macrophages were subjected to hypoxia/nutrient deprivation or ox-LDL, and conditioned media were applied to endothelial and smooth muscle cells to assess TNFRSF1A-dependent cytotoxicity, NF-κB/MAPK activation, lipid accumulation, and cytokine release. RESULTS: Single-cell and spatial analyses revealed a conserved plaque architecture: myeloid cells enriched in the lipid core, mural and endothelial cells at the periphery. Five endothelial, eight mural, and six macrophage subtypes showed distinct spatial and functional features. Central to these interactions, TNF-TNFRSF1A emerged as a central signaling axis linking macrophages, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells. Microenvironmental stress amplified macrophage TNF-α secretion, leading to promoting TNFRSF1A-dependent vascular cell death, NF-κB/MAPK activation, and foam cell formation. Mechanistically, ox-LDL upregulated increased macrophage CD36 and TREM2, while TNFRSF1A knockdown mitigated lipid accumulation, cytokine release, and downstream signaling. CONCLUSIONS: These findings delineate the spatial and functional landscape of AS plaques and reveal a conserved, spatially constrained mechanism: macrophage-derived TNF-α drives TNFRSF1A-dependent vascular injury, inflammatory amplification, and foam cell formation, highlighting this axis as a promising therapeutic target for atherosclerotic diseases.

Healthy Dietary Patterns and Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Cancer Survivors: A Prospective Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of noncancer mortality among cancer survivors. The potential influence of healthy dietary patterns on CVD risk among cancer survivors remains poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the association between healthy dietary patterns and incident CVD among cancer survivors. METHODS: We analyzed data from 8,716 cancer survivors initially free of CVD in the UK Biobank cohort. We used 24-hour dietary recall data to calculate 8 dietary pattern scores. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risks models were used to investigate the association between dietary patterns and incident CVD. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 12.3 (Q1-Q3: 11.6-13.0) years, 1,116 individuals experienced incident CVD events. When comparing the top quintile with the bottom quintile, HRs (95% CI) for total CVD were 0.72 (0.58-0.88) for Mediterranean diet score, 0.74 (0.61-0.89) for Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to stop Hypertension Diet Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay score, 0.63 (0.52-0.76) for Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010, 0.65 (0.53-0.79) for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension score, 0.82 (0.68-0.99) for healthful Plant-Based Diet Index, 0.67 (0.55-0.80) for reversed energy-adjusted diet inflammatory index, and 0.80 (0.67-0.96) for healthy low-fat diet score. The findings remain robust after fitting the generalized propensity score model. At age 45, participants with the highest adherence to healthy dietary patterns gained an estimated life expectancy of 1.66 to 3.32 years more than those with the lowest adherence. CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to healthy dietary patterns is associated with reduced CVD risk among cancer survivors, underscoring the potential for diet to support cardio-oncology care.

Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

recs.title: KLHL3-Cab39 Disruption Drives WNK4-Independent Hyperkalemic Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Familial hyperkalemic hypertension, also known as pseudohypoaldosteronism type II (PHAII), is characterized by hypertension and hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis and involves dysregulation of the KLHL3 (Kelch-like 3)-cullin3 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, affecting WNK1/4 (with-no-lysine kinase 1/4)-mediated SPAK (Ste20-related proline/alanine-rich kinase)/OSR1 (oxidative stress response kinase 1)-NCC (Na+-Cl- cotransporter) signaling. How KLHL3 phosphorylation mutations modulate this pathway remains poorly defined. METHODS: We generated knock-in mouse models expressing phosphomimetic (S486D) or phosphodefective (S486G) mutations at Klhl3 S486 (homologous to human S433). Blood pressure, serum and urine biochemistries, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, coimmunoprecipitation, in vitro ubiquitination assays, and molecular docking were performed. Klhl3 S486G mice were crossed with Wnk4-/- mice to test WNK4 dependence. RESULTS: Both knock-in strains exhibited typical PHAII features despite unchanged KLHL3 levels, with enhanced SPAK/OSR1-NCC phosphorylation, increased Cab39 levels, and unchanged WNK1/4 expression. Under high-salt loading, Klhl3 S486 knock-in mice maintained severe PHAII phenotypes, with persistently elevated Cab39 and NCC levels despite decreased WNK4 expression. Critically, Wnk4 deletion failed to rescue PHAII phenotypes in Klhl3 S486G mice, demonstrating that Klhl3 S486 mutations drive PHAII independently of WNK4. In vitro, human KLHL3 S433D/S433G mutations reduced KLHL3-Cab39 association and Cab39 ubiquitination, with a corresponding increase in Cab39 abundance. Deletion mapping identified KLHL3 residues 428 to 437 and Cab39 residues 314 to 324 as key determinants of the KLHL3-Cab39 association. CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the integrity of Ser486 itself, rather than its phosphorylation state, is required for KLHL3-mediated Cab39 ubiquitination and define a WNK4-independent PHAII mechanism driven by impaired Cab39 degradation and consequent SPAK/OSR1-Na+-Cl- cotransporter activation.

recs.title: Cardiomyocyte-expressed TGFβ programs early heart maturation and adult myocyte identity.
recs.abstract: Transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) is a secreted factor sequestered in the extracellular matrix (ECM), but its role in developing mouse heart maturation is unknown. Here we show that cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Tgfb1, Tgfb2 and Tgfb3 genes (TGFβ ligands) in the developing heart results in cardiac dysfunction by 6 weeks of age, altered fibroblast activity, abnormal ECM properties and endothelial and immune changes. Gene profiling reveals defective cardiomyocyte/fibroblast maturation with cardiomyocyte ectopic skeletal muscle gene expression beginning at embryonic day 17.5 (E17.5). Cardiomyocyte deletion of Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 or Smad2/Smad3 does not phenocopy Tgfb1/2/3 deletion, suggesting that cardiomyocyte TGFβ acts through non-myocytes to regulate heart maturation. Similarly, Col1a2-/-;Col6a2-/- mice with reduced ECM stiffness, cardiomyocyte-specific Itgb1 deletion reducing ECM mechanosensing and Tcf21-/- embryos lacking cardiac fibroblasts fail to reproduce ectopic skeletal muscle gene expression. Thus, embryonic cardiomyocyte-derived TGFβ signals to non-myocytes to establish an environment that directs cardiomyocyte maturation and identity.

Sudden Cardiac Death in Firefighters From the United States: A 16-Year Postmortem Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is the leading cause of duty-related death among firefighters. Understanding postmortem cardiovascular abnormalities associated with SCD is critical to guiding fire service cardiovascular disease screening and prevention programs. METHODS: This study included US firefighters who had a duty-related death over a 16-year period (1999-2014) with available postmortem reports (autopsy/medical examiner reports). Cases were systematically reviewed to identify cases of SCD. For each SCD case, the primary etiology of SCD was adjudicated by experts in sports cardiology and cardiovascular pathology. RESULTS: Postmortem evaluations were available for 794 of 2100 (37.8%) on-duty firefighter deaths over the study period (average age, 44±13 years; age range, 17-82 years; 4.0% women). A total of 312 of 794 (39.3%) firefighter deaths were adjudicated as SCD. A total of 255 of 312 (81.8%) SCD events were attributable to coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease or hypertensive heart disease, which both are associated with traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The leading etiology of SCD among young firefighters (aged <40 years) was also coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease (24/50 [48.0%]). Of firefighters who had an exertional SCD event thought to be secondary to coronary artery disease (n=97), a total of 62 of 91 (68.1%) had severe fixed coronary stenosis, while 29 of 91 (31.9%) demonstrated acute plaque rupture/thrombosis. CONCLUSIONS: More than 80% of on-duty SCD events among US firefighters are due to coronary artery disease and hypertensive heart disease that may be prevented by early disease identification and risk factor modification. Future studies should assess the efficacy of more rigorous firefighter cardiovascular disease screening and management practices.

Pacing Related Conduction Delay as an Indicator of Intramural Site of Origin of Focal Ventricular Arrhythmias.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The diagnosis of intramural focal ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be challenging and is often made in retrospect after a long ineffective procedure. OBJECTIVES: In this cohort of patients, we aim to assess the value of pace-mapping (PM), stimulus-QRS interval (S-QRS interval), and electrogram (EGM)-QRS intervals to identify the site of origin (SOO) of focal VAs. METHODS: In a consecutive series of 46 patients with frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), activation mapping and PM were performed to identify VA target sites. VA target sites were defined as sites with matching PM (≥10/12 leads) and/or sites with the earliest activation time. S-QRS interval and bipolar activation time at target sites were assessed and correlated with acute outcomes. If ablation at a target site failed, alternative sites were sought in adjacent anatomical structures. An intramural origin was defined as a VA with early activation time without a matching PM. RESULTS: Matching PMs were identified for 32 VAs in 30 of the 46 patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed at the target site/PVC level and demonstrated that a mismatch between S-QRS and EGM-QRS of >26 milliseconds distinguished effective from ineffective ablation sites with a matching PM (area under the curve: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.94-1; sensitivity: 100%; specificity: 88.9%). A mismatch was present in 9 patients, and radiofrequency ablation failed in 8/9 of them. Alternate sites with early activation times (-48.4 ± 37.39 milliseconds) without matching PM, where radiofrequency eliminated the PVCs, were identified in 5/8 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Conduction delay with matching PMs but late activation indicates a deeper SOO. A cutoff value of >26 milliseconds between S-QRS and EGM-QRS intervals identified deeper-seated VA target sites. This required further mapping to identify alternative ablation sites. A matching PM may not always be indicative of the SOO in patients with PVCs.

recs.title: Salt-Sensitive Hypertension Begins With Intracellular K+ and Water Loss.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Na+ and water overload due to inappropriately low renal salt and water excretion is considered the root cause of salt-sensitive hypertension. However, experimental renal and psoriasis hypertension are characterized by chronic predisposition to dehydration. We tested the validity of this alternative hypertension due to loss of water theory in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) salt-sensitive hypertension. METHODS: We tested the effect of DOCA (25 mg pellet) in mice on a low Na+ diet (0.02%-0.03%) with tap water, or with Na+ in their drinking water (1% NaCl or 1.44% NaHCO3), on body Na+, K+, and water content 2, 6, and 12 days after treatment initiation. We monitored blood pressure with radio-telemetry, food and water intake, and renal electrolyte and water excretion. RESULTS: At day 2, DOCA NaCl-treated mice elevated blood pressure during a state of isolated body K+ and water loss, indicating substantial intracellular dehydration. Although increasing their fluid intake and urine output, the mice reduced the excretion of free water, indicating renal water conservation. At days 6 and 12, secondary Na+ retention occurred, which replaced the amount of K+ lost and corrected the dehydration, albeit at the expense of an intracellular Na+/K+ redistribution disorder. DOCA NaHCO3-treated mice with Na+-resistant blood pressure showed a comparable Na+/K+ redistribution disorder, but without accompanying early dehydration due to earlier replacement of lost K+ by Na+. CONCLUSIONS: Experimental DOCA salt-sensitive hypertension initiates with a systemic water conservation response in the face of K+-driven intracellular water loss. Both dehydration and blood pressure increase could be causally treated by oral K+ supplementation.

recs.title: Calcium Fracture Detection by Optical Coherence Tomography Versus Intravascular Ultrasound Following Intravascular Lithotripsy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Calcium fracture is a metric used to assess lesion preparation success. We have shown previously that optical coherence tomography (OCT) misses approximately half of these fractures. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is the most commonly used intravascular imaging modality. The sensitivity of IVUS for detecting calcium fractures after intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to assess the frequency and characteristics of calcium fracture observed on IVUS in comparison to OCT and gold standard micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) using heavily calcified coronary artery cadaveric vessels. METHODS: In an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric hearts (15 coronary lesions), OCT, IVUS, and micro-CT were obtained before and after IVL coronary artery treatment. Fracture detection rates and appearance patterns were compared across modalities. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated OCT-measured fracture width thresholds for IVUS detectability. RESULTS: Compared with micro-CT, OCT and IVUS significantly underestimated fracture occurrence, but OCT demonstrated higher detection sensitivity than IVUS (P < 0.05 by McNemar's test). Narrow linear nondisplaced fractures identified on OCT were frequently undetectable on IVUS or appeared as subtle hyperechoic shadows. Fracture width was strongly associated with IVUS detectability; fracture width >115 μm on OCT were identified by IVUS with excellent diagnostic performance (area under the curve: 0.99 [95% CI: 0.98-1.00], sensitivity 100%, specificity 92%). CONCLUSIONS: OCT and IVUS underestimate the occurrence of IVL-induced calcium fractures compared with micro-CT, with IVUS demonstrating lower sensitivity than OCT. IVUS detectability is strongly dependent on fracture width. Absence of visible fracture on either OCT or IVUS does not exclude calcium modification.

Combined bipolar and unipolar voltage mapping to identify epicardial breakthrough regions after pulsed field ablation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The utility of unipolar voltage (UV) mapping for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains undetermined. OBJECTIVE: This study assessed combined bipolar voltage (BV) and UV mapping for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions after pulsed field ablation (PFA). METHODS: Thirty patients with atrial fibrillation underwent initial PFA-PVI with a pentaspline catheter under fluoroscopic guidance. Within the isolated PV antrum (BV <0.1 mV), transmurally ablated regions and epicardial breakthrough regions were defined by UV <1.08 mV and UV ≥1.08 mV, respectively. Unipolar electrogram features were investigated to identify epicardial breakthrough regions. RESULTS: Seventeen patients had 27 epicardial breakthrough regions, yielding 276 local unipolar electrograms (QR pattern: n=160; RS pattern: n=116). QR electrograms were distributed broadly within the isolated PV, whereas RS electrograms occurred exclusively around the isolation boundary. QR electrograms, indicating possible epicardial breakthrough, had significantly higher UV amplitudes than RS electrograms (median: 1.64 vs. 0.70 mV; P<0.001). The UV amplitude cutoff distinguishing these morphologies was 1.15 mV (sensitivity, 91.9%; specificity, 84.5%; area under the curve [AUC], 0.922; P<0.001). Among 245 local unipolar electrograms around the isolation boundary, excluding QR electrograms, RS electrograms had higher UV amplitudes and steeper negative intrinsic deflection slopes than non-RS electrograms, suggesting possible intramural conduction gaps. Respective cutoffs were 0.48 mV (sensitivity, 83.6%; specificity, 86.8%; AUC, 0.923; P<0.001) and 0.020 mV/ms (sensitivity, 97.4%; specificity, 94.5%; AUC, 0.992; P<0.001). CONCLUSION: Combined BV and UV mapping provides additional information for identifying epicardial breakthrough regions at PFA application sites.

Artificial Intelligence Detection of Aortic Valve Calcification on Routine Noncontrast Chest CT: A Real-World Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine noncontrast chest computed tomography (CT) may reveal aortic valve calcification (AVC) outside aortic stenosis evaluation. Its prevalence, burden, and documentation remain uncertain. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable systematic detection. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to evaluate AVC prevalence and burden, clinical correlates, radiology documentation, and AI-assisted case finding. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study screened 511 consecutive noncontrast, non-electrocardiographically gated chest CT examinations in adults aged ≥50 years. After 15 protocol exclusions and 56 software-designated nonevaluable examinations, 440 underwent quantification by 2 blinded readers. AVC was defined as >10 AU using a 130-Hounsfield-unit threshold adjusted for blood-pool attenuation and image noise when needed. Locked HealthAVC V1.0 was a secondary comparator. RESULTS: Manual quantification identified AVC in 172 of 440 scans (39.1%; 95% CI: 34.6%-43.7%); 97 of 440 (22.0%) had ≥100 AU. Inter-reader agreement at >10 AU was 99.5% (kappa = 0.990). Age (adjusted OR: 1.92 per 5 years; 95% CI: 1.63-2.26) and male sex (adjusted OR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.32-3.30) were associated with AVC. Reports documented 27 of 172 positive scans (15.7%; 95% CI: 11.0%-21.9%). AI detected 169 of 172 manually confirmed cases (98.3%) among 440 evaluable scans, including 142 of 145 undocumented cases. Of 496 submitted scans, 56 (11.3%) were nonevaluable. End-to-end sensitivity counting positive rejected scans as missed was 89.9%. Among 86 AI-positive patients with echocardiography, 10 (11.6%) had mild-or-greater aortic stenosis. CONCLUSIONS: AVC was common but infrequently documented on routine chest CT. AI detected most cases among evaluable scans; 11.3% were nonevaluable, yielding 89.9% end-to-end sensitivity. Prospective studies should assess clinical pathways.

recs.title: Testosterone, Testosterone Replacement Therapy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Contemporary Review.
recs.abstract: Whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease, and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified, remain contested, while US labeling has moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. We conducted a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, searching MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture, and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. Noninferiority over 3 years should not be read as long-term clinical equivalence. Safe use of testosterone replacement therapy requires appropriate patient selection, distinction between pathologic hypogonadism and functional or age-associated low testosterone, mapping of each recommendation to its evidentiary tier, and close multidisciplinary collaboration.

recs.title: Young-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: Prevalence and Predictors of Adverse Long-Term Outcomes.
Trends in Oral Anticoagulant Prescribing for Atrial Fibrillation and Active Cancer in UK Primary Care.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation is essential in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and cancer, but recent real-world evidence on oral anticoagulant (OAC) use remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to describe recent OAC-prescribing trends and identify factors associated with OAC initiation in patients with AF and active cancer in UK primary care. METHODS: Using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, we identified patients aged ≥50 years with incident AF (cohort entry) between 2010 and 2023 and active cancer diagnosed in the year before cohort entry. We calculated OAC initiation rates in the year following AF diagnosis among eligible patients (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2) using Poisson regression, overall and stratified by OAC type, age, sex, and cancer characteristics. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify factors associated with OAC initiation. RESULTS: Among 12,254 eligible patients, 6,940 (56.6%) initiated an OAC. OAC initiation rates rose from 89 per 100 person-years in 2010 to 385 per 100 person-years in 2023 (adjusted rate ratio: 4.32; 95% CI: 3.78-4.93), driven by increased direct oral anticoagulant prescribing. By 2023, apixaban and edoxaban predominated. OAC initiation did not differ by age and sex but was less common in patients with lung cancer (HR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.67-0.82), metastatic cancer (HR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.51-0.87), and dementia (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.64-0.88). CONCLUSIONS: In the last decade, OAC initiation has substantially increased among eligible patients with AF and active cancer, driven by direct oral anticoagulant uptake. However, OAC initiation remained lower among patients with lung cancer, metastatic cancer, or specific comorbidities.

recs.title: Defining cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic progression by a cardiovascular endpoint: a built-in circularity.

A Framework for Cardiovascular Disease Polygenic Risk Score Counseling.
Pulsed Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Pulmonary Index of Microcirculatory Resistance: A Novel Hemodynamic Index for Invasively Assessing the Pulmonary Microvasculature.
Effectiveness of digital health interventions for care integration in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
recs.abstract: AIM: To assess the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) supporting care integration for coronary artery disease (CAD) in improving health outcomes compared to usual care. METHODS: For this systematic review, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, EBSCO Psychology and Behavioural Sciences Collection, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1 January 1995 to 5 November 2025. We included studies reporting primary data on DHIs supporting care integration for patients with CAD. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and readmissions, and CVD events. Secondary endpoints were the control of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted random-effects meta-analyses in RevMan and assessed risk of bias with Cochrane's RoB tools. RESULTS: We included 72 studies (23,111 participants), assessing 45 in the meta-analysis. All DHIs supported person-centred care integration (n=72) while few DHIs addressed clinical care integration (n=22), professional integration (n=12) and functional integration (n=22). Compared to usual care, DHIs supporting care integration had significant reductions in the odds of CVD events (OR: 0.74 [0.59, 0.92], df=5, p=0.02), but not in all-cause mortality or readmissions. CONCLUSIONS: Although this review shows that DHIs supporting care integration were associated with reduced CVD events compared to usual care, the current evidence remains concentrated primarily on person-centred care integration, with limited studies evaluating broader dimensions of care integration at organisational and systemic levels. These findings highlight the important evidence gaps of DHIs in supporting more comprehensive and system-level integration in cardiovascular care. Further research is necessary to understand the influence of DHI modality and function on effectiveness of care integration.

recs.title: Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic implications of abdominal obesity and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in patients with type 2 diabetes who have a normal body mass index remain unclear. METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 323 029 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index (<23 kg/m2) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2023, from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Abdominal obesity was defined using sex-specific waist circumference thresholds (≥90 cm for men, ≥80 cm for women). MVPA was assessed through standardized self-reported questionnaires administered during routine health screenings. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure. RESULTS: Among the study population, 34 033 (10.5%) had abdominal obesity. During a median follow-up of 6.0 years (interquartile range, 2.6-9.0 years), abdominal obesity was associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.09-1.17]). Among patients with abdominal obesity, regular MVPA after diagnosis (27.1%) was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted HR 0.74 [95% CI, 0.68-0.80]), all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.72 [95% CI, 0.65-0.80]), ischemic stroke (adjusted HR 0.77 [95% CI, 0.66-0.89]), and hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted HR 0.75 [95% CI, 0.60-0.93]). The cardiovascular protective effects of MVPA were consistent regardless of statin or antidiabetic medication use. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index, abdominal obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Regular engagement in MVPA showed consistent cardiovascular benefits in this population, irrespective of pharmacotherapy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT07071545.

recs.title: When the Conversation Is the Intervention: Serious Illness Communication Skills in Adult Congenital Heart Disease.
The future of PFA in cardiac ablation procedures.
recs.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as a major development in catheter ablation, with increasing clinical adoption driven by procedural efficiency and a favorable safety profile compared with thermal energies. This article summarizes the future directions of PFA in electrophysiology, focusing on technological innovation, and how these advances are expected to expand PFA clinical indications. Additionally, this article provides a perspective on current gaps and future challenges of PFA. A perspective on future developments in new waveforms, catheter architectures, and integration with electroanatomical mapping systems for PFA is summarized. The document discusses novel waveform configurations and catheter design concepts that may improve lesion quality, procedural versatility, and safety. Additionally, this article also reviews how parallel advances in electroanatomical mapping integration, artificial intelligence, and robotic navigation are expected to enhance procedural guidance and enable individualized therapy. This manuscript summarizes the potential applications of PFA beyond pulmonary vein isolation and how emerging evidence supports its feasibility for linear atrial lesions, substrate modification, treatment of complex atrial tachycardias, and ventricular arrhythmia ablation. In addition, this article provides insights on how PFA may facilitate catheter ablation in new patient populations including elderly patients and those with higher procedural risks. Finally, this manuscript provides an outlook at major remaining challenges and knowledge gaps for PFA. The lack of homogenous procedural endpoints definitions and lesion durability assessment are discussed. Furthermore, this article highlights the need for standardized terminology and reporting in an environment where the high heterogeneity between available commercial systems complicates comparison across technologies.

recs.title: Substance Use-Associated Infective Endocarditis Mortality for 2018 to 2024: A Ray of Hope.
Associations between vascular aging and 12 lipid composite indices: A large cross-sectional study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Vascular aging is an important antecedent of cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet affordable, widely available biomarkers for its early detection remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive value of 12 lipid composite indices for vascular aging in a large cross-sectional sample of adults from Shenzhen, China. METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of 5518 adults screened in Shenzhen (2021-2023), vascular aging (baPWV ≥ 1400 cm/s) was evaluated against 12 indices (TyG, TyG-BMI, RC, TG/HDL-C, AC, AIP, LCI, CRI-II, NHR, MHR, LHR, PHR) derived from routine laboratory and hematological data. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression across four sequentially adjusted models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) and two-piece linear models were used to evaluate dose-response relationships and thresholds. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis compared the discriminative performance of each index alone and in combination with age. Subgroup and interaction analyses examined effect modification by BMI, gender, age, hypertension, and diabetes. RESULTS: All 12 indices remained independently associated with vascular aging after multivariable adjustment. In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), each 1-unit increase in TyG was associated with an odds ratio (OR) of 2.21 (95% CI, 1.88-2.58; P < 0.001), and individuals in the highest TyG quartile (Q4) had an OR of 4.27 (95% CI, 3.16-5.77) compared with Q1; other indices showed similar effects. RCS analyses revealed significant nonlinear positive associations for several indices, with risk increasing below these thresholds. Individually, the indices had modest discrimination (AUC range, 0.562-0.726), but adding age improved all models; the TyG + age model achieved the best performance (AUC, 0.850; 95% CI, 0.838-0.862). BMI, gender, and diabetes status significantly modified several associations. CONCLUSIONS: Among the 12 lipid composite indices evaluated, TyG-especially when combined with age-demonstrated the strongest predictive value for vascular aging in this large Chinese population, suggesting it may serve as a low-incremental-cost preliminary screening marker. However, prospective validation and intervention trials are needed to confirm the threshold and to determine whether lowering TyG attenuates vascular aging and subsequent CVD risk.

recs.title: Acute effects of cardioneuroablation on ventricular arrhythmia inducibility and refractoriness in patients with functional bradyarrhythmias. The Roman 4 study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardioneuroablation (CNA) is a promising method to treat functional bradyarrhythmias. However, whether CNA-induced decrease in the parasympathetic drive to the heart may occur proarrhythmic in the future is not known. OBJECTIVE: To assess acute effects of CNA-induced total vagal denervation on QT interval as well as invasively measured ventricular effective refractory period (VERP), ventricular action potential duration (VAPD) and vulnerability to ventricular arrhythmias. METHODS: CNA was performed using anatomical approach by means of electro-anatomical mapping and intracardiac echocardiography. Intra-procedural efficacy was assessed using extracardiac vagal stimulation. QTc and QTd intervals were measured from surface ECG. VAPD and VERP were measured from ablation electrode in right ventricle. Measurements were performed at four time-points: at baseline, immediately after CNA, after atropine injection, and finally after isoproterenol bolus. RESULTS: 80 patients (51 females, mean age 42 ± 14 years) underwent CNA. Polymorphic ventricular tachyarrhythmias were induced in 2 females who had pre-existing cardiac conditions. Changes in QTc depended on the method used for correction. Using the Bazett formula, QTc was significantly prolonged, however using the Framingham, Fridericia and Hodges corrections, these changes were much less pronounced or non-significant. QTd remained unchanged across all measurements. The VERP and VAPD values remained unchanged after CNA and after atropine whereas they became significantly shorter following isoproterenol injection. CONCLUSION: The present study did not demonstrate evidence of acute electrophysiological changes suggesting increased ventricular arrhythmogenicity after CNA in patients without structural heart disease. However, long-term follow-up is needed to confirm lack of proarrhythmic effects of CNA.

recs.title: Severe Atrial Compression Detected During Electroanatomical Mapping.
Hypertension and Subclinical Vascular Damage After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloHSCT) face a higher risk of premature cardiovascular disease that may partly be explained by hypertension. OBJECTIVES: The authors studied the prevalence of hypertension in alloHSCT survivors at least 1 year post-transplant. METHODS: Two hundred survivors were clinically screened for hypertension. Hypertension was defined according to established ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) thresholds. Subclinical vascular damage was assessed through carotid intima-media thickness by ultrasonography of the carotid arteries, pulse wave velocity, and renal function. RESULTS: Of the 200 patients, 168 (84%) completed the 24-hour ABPM. The median age was 57 years (IQR: 46.3-65.0; range: 18-75). Of the 168 patients, 90 patients (53.6%) had hypertension, of which 26 (15.5%) were newly diagnosed, and 56 (33.3%) were untreated. Hypertensive patients by ABPM tended to be older (median 58 [IQR: 49-67] vs 55.5 [IQR: 39.75-64] years; P = 0.060), had a higher intima-media thickness (0.84 ± 0.25 vs 0.76 ± 0.26 mm; P = 0.009), higher pulse wave velocity values (9.0 ± 2.3 vs 7.3 ± 1.6 m/s; P < 0.001), and lower mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (72.3 ± 18.7 vs 80.4 ± 22.5 mL/min/1.73 m2; P = 0.010) compared to normotensive patients. In the logistic regression model, both age in years (OR: 1.03; 95% CI: 1.01-1.05; P = 0.019) and family history of cardiovascular disease and/or premature death (OR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.17-4.44; P = 0.016) were independently associated with hypertension. CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension is highly prevalent, underrecognized, and undertreated in alloHSCT survivors and is cross-sectionally associated with subclinical vascular and renal organ damage.

recs.title: Letter by Shui et al Regarding Article, "Breast Cancer Reveals Latent BMPR2-Related Susceptibility to Pulmonary Hypertension".
Redefining Noninvasive Post-Transplant Surveillance: A Bayesian Decision Framework for Donor-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Heart Transplantation.
CATHETER ABLATION VERSUS SHAM FOR SYMPTOMATIC ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results. OBJECTIVE: To synthesise sham-controlled trials of AF ablation and identify why QoL results differ. METHODS: We searched databases and registries for randomized trials of catheter ablation versus sham in symptomatic AF. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, pooled using a Bayesian random-effects model. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. RESULTS: Four trials (468 patients) were eligible; three (448 patients) were pooled. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Heterogeneity (τ 8.2 points, I2 85.3%) was largely attributed to PVI-SHAM-AF, which differed from the other trials in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring and assessment of blinding; without it, the difference was 18.9 points (6.7 to 31.4). Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL. CONCLUSION: Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. Trials differ in population, monitoring, and estimator, not direction of effect.

recs.title: Finerenone-Empagliflozin Combination Therapy in Apparent Resistant Hypertension: A CONFIDENCE Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (aTRH) is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with type 2 diabetes and predicts worse outcomes. Spironolactone, the established fourth-line agent, is limited by hyperkalemia in CKD. OBJECTIVES: This analysis assessed whether finerenone plus empagliflozin lowers blood pressure (BP) meaningfully in aTRH, and whether aTRH modifies these agents' efficacy and safety. METHODS: Post hoc analysis of CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), a double-blind randomized trial of finerenone, empagliflozin, or both in CKD with albuminuria and type 2 diabetes. aTRH was BP ≥130/80 mm Hg on 3 antihypertensive drugs, or ≥4 drugs regardless of BP. Mixed models and logistic regression identified predictors of BP response. RESULTS: Of the 796 participants, 307 (39%) had aTRH; they were older, more obese, and had more atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, higher albuminuria, and higher systolic BP (140.9 vs 131.5 mm Hg) but similar estimated glomerular filtration rate (53 vs 55 mL/min/1.73 m2). Combination therapy lowered systolic BP more than either monotherapy. Independent predictors of a ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP fall were aTRH (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.25) and higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR: 1.15 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: 1.05-1.26); diuretic use and albuminuria were not. The aTRH effect was treatment-independent (interaction P = 0.21). Adverse events were more frequent with aTRH (63.8% vs 51.1%), yet on combination therapy hyperkalemia was less frequent (11.2% vs 17.5%). CONCLUSIONS: aTRH affected approximately 40% of participants and marked a higher-risk phenotype responsive to finerenone-empagliflozin, with BP reductions comparable to spironolactone but without the excess hyperkalemia that limits its use in CKD.

recs.title: Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Novel Prognostic Marker.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort. METHODS: Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management. RESULTS: In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P < 0.001) compared with patients with low L-ECV. High L-ECV independently predicted the outcome even after multivariable adjustment accounting for TR severity, biventricular ejection fraction, and pulmonary pressure (adjusted HR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.03-3.18; P = 0.030). Finally, L-ECV showed incremental prognostic value compared with TRI-SCORE when assessed in a nested Cox model. CONCLUSIONS: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

recs.title: Which Method to Measure Arterial Stiffness: The Impossible Dilemma?
Impact of Surrounding Fluid Impedance on Contact Sensing Vulnerabilities and Staining Depth During Pulsed Field Ablation.
Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a heritable cardiac disorder commonly linked to alterations in desmosomal proteins. While desmosomal dysfunction is a recognized pathogenic mechanism, the early molecular remodeling that precedes clinical manifestations remains unclear. Here we used a mouse model with inducible cardiomyocyte-specific knockout of Pkp2 (encoding plakophilin-2) and performed time-resolved mass spectrometry-based proteomics to map disease progression from early PKP2 loss to structural remodeling. Molecular changes preceded phenotypic abnormalities, and spatial asymmetry was evident, with earlier and more pronounced proteome remodeling in the right ventricle despite comparable PKP2 depletion in both ventricles. Downregulation of protein networks spanning desmosomes, sarcomeres and mitochondria suggests their functional coupling, with mitochondrial remodeling emerging as an early and progressively worsening feature. Intervention with honokiol attenuated changes across the major protein networks, highlighting mitochondrial pathways as promising therapeutic targets and honokiol as a potential strategy to delay arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy progression. Our findings provide critical insights into the concealed stage of disease progression and identify molecular targets for early intervention.

recs.title: Response by Mougin et al to Letter Regarding Article, "Breast Cancer Reveals Latent BMPR2-Related Susceptibility to Pulmonary Hypertension".
Zero-fluoroscopy approach to left atrial appendage closure using intracardiac echo guidance.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) with the Watchman™ device is typically performed with the use of transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and fluoroscopy. LAAC guided by intracardiac echo (ICE) without the use of fluoroscopy has not been previously described. OBJECTIVE: In this series, we describe the safety and feasibility of Watchman™ implantation using only ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy. METHODS: 214 patients undergoing LAAC with the Watchman FLX™ or Watchman FLX™ Pro device and using a planned fluoroscopy-free approach were studied. ICE was used for echocardiographic imaging in all cases. TEE was not used in any cases. Fluoroscopy was used as a bail-out approach when it was felt to be clinically necessary by the operator. Peri-procedural, 45-day, and 1-year efficacy and safety outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: In 203/214 patients (94.8%), LAAC was completed without the use of fluoroscopy. Bail-out fluoroscopy was required in 11/214 patients (5.1%). Successful device implantation was completed in 212/214 patients (99.1%). The rate of any peri-device leak at 45 days post-procedure was 11.6%. Procedural complications were limited to one pericardial effusion and one case of ventricular tachycardia. CONCLUSION: LAAC with the Watchman™ device using ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy appears to be safe and effective. The rates of procedural success, complications, and peri-device leaks on 45 day follow up were consistent with that seen in pivotal clinical trials. Further studies are needed to assess the broader applicability of this technique.

recs.title: Treatment of paroxysmal and persistent atrial fibrillation with pulsed field ablation.
recs.abstract: Pulsed field ablation has emerged as a novel energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering preferential myocardial ablation with a favourable safety profile. Contemporary paroxysmal AF clinical studies demonstrate 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence in approximately 75-85% of patients, with major complication rates generally ranging from 1 to 3%. Compared with thermal ablation, PFA offers comparable efficacy and streamlined procedural workflows. In persistent AF, PVI remains the foundation of ablation, while additional adjunctive strategies are increasingly evaluated. Current evidence suggests that PFA can achieve 12-month arrhythmia-free outcomes generally ranging from approximately 60-75% in persistent AF populations. Major procedure-related complications typically occur in <3% of cases, supporting the feasibility of broader lesion sets with an acceptable safety profile. However, the incremental benefit of adjunctive ablation beyond PVI and the optimal lesion set for persistent AF remain to be assessed further Outcome assessment after PFA requires consideration of evolving endpoints. The clinical relevance of the traditional post-ablation blanking period is being re-evaluated, while continuous rhythm monitoring and AF burden are increasingly incorporated alongside conventional recurrence endpoints. Patient-reported outcomes are an important component of PFA evaluation. Compared with thermal ablation, PFA is associated with improved procedural tolerability, reduced analgesic requirements, rapid recovery, and the potential for same-day discharge. These features, together with favourable efficacy and safety outcomes, may contribute to broader adoption of PFA across both paroxysmal and persistent AF populations.

recs.title: Micro- and nanoplastics in acute coronary thrombosis: exposure, enrichment, or a dual mechanism?
Low-grade inflammation and cardiovascular events among patients with chronic kidney disease.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Chronic inflammation is associated with cardiovascular disease in the general population, but data on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. We sought to assess whether systemic low-grade inflammation is independently associated with cardiovascular events in CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, with or without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). METHODS: CKD-REIN is a prospective cohort study of adults with CKD stages 2-5, conducted in 40 French nephrology outpatient facilities. Baseline high-sensitivity plasma C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was centrally measured using an immunoturbidimetric method. Systemic low-grade inflammation was defined as hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models estimated cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death) or hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). RESULTS: We included 2078 patients: 67% men, mean (SD) age 67(13) years, mean eGFR 36(12) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38% with history of ASCVD, median hs-CRP concentration 2.4 mg/L (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.1). After median follow-up of 5 years, 171 patients had a MACE and 207 had HHF. After controlling for potential confounders, a twofold increase in hs-CRP was associated with a 12% (95% CI 0-26) higher cause-specific hazard of MACE and a 26% (95% CI 13-40) higher cause-specific hazard of HHF. CONCLUSION: In CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, systemic low-grade inflammation, measured through hs-CRP, is associated with occurrence of cardiovascular events independently of traditional risk factors, including a history of ASCVD.

recs.title: Incidence of Dementia and Subsequent Outcomes in Patients With Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dementia and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist; however, the relationship between these conditions is not fully explored. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study were to: 1) compare dementia incidence in newly-diagnosed patients with HF or matched non-HF controls; and 2) examine risk factors for and outcomes after dementia diagnosis in HF patients. METHODS: In community-dwelling residents (aged 40-80 years), we compared incident dementia in those with new-onset HF vs age/sex, and cardiovascular risk factor/disease-matched non-HF controls. In those with HF, we examined time-varying dementia onset as the exposure with outcomes of mortality and hospitalization. We also compared physician visits after vs before dementia diagnosis. RESULTS: Among 211,548 outpatients with HF (median 68 [60-75] years, 41.2% female), time-dependent HRs for dementia were 1.42 (95% CI: 1.38-1.47) at 5 years and 1.31 (95% CI: 1.27-1.35) at 10 years compared to non-HF controls. Prior stroke or transient ischemia attack (HR: 1.41; 95% CI: 1.33-1.50) and hospital frailty risk score >10 vs <5 (HR: 1.93; 95% CI: 1.77-2.09) were important predictors of dementia (both P < 0.001). Incident dementia was associated with higher multivariable-adjusted hazards of all-cause mortality (HR: 2.44; 95% CI: 2.40-2.49) and all-cause hospitalization (HR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.58-1.69) in outpatients with HF (all P < 0.001). Rates of outpatient physician visits with primary care, internal medicine, cardiologists (post/pre-rate ratio range 1.08-1.19), and geriatricians (post/prerate ratio 10.70; all P < 0.001) were higher after (versus before) dementia onset. CONCLUSIONS: Incident HF was associated with higher risk of incident dementia. Dementia onset was associated with higher rates of outpatient physician visits and increased risk of adverse outcomes.

recs.title: Evaluating Patients for Renal Denervation: A Pragmatic Approach.
Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation. OBJECTIVE: To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD. METHODS: This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared. RESULTS: Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications. CONCLUSION: The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.

recs.title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials. METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding. RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

recs.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction. METHODS: In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001). CONCLUSION: Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

recs.title: Association of Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat Infiltration With Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence After Pulsed-Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration (inFAT) is an emerging imaging phenotype of the atrial substrate in atrial fibrillation (AF). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate inFAT and peri-left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) using artificial intelligence-based CT analysis software (ADAS 3D) and to assess their association with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after persistent AF ablation. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 59 patients who underwent pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. inFAT and LA-EAT were quantified using a semi-automated algorithm. Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association of inFAT and LA-EAT with recurrence. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed after stratification according to the tertile of each parameter. RESULTS: During a median follow-up period of 11.2 [6.4-11.9] months, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 21 (36%) patients. The inFAT volume was significantly greater in patients with recurrence than those without (1.25 [0.78-1.53] vs. 0.72 [0.45-1.09] cm3, p=0.021). In contrast, LA-EAT volume was comparable between the groups (21.8 [13.7-30.4] vs. 17.5 [14.1-26.8] cm3, p=0.419). In Cox regression analysis, higher inFAT was significantly associated with recurrence, whereas LA-EAT was not significantly associated (inFAT: hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-3.27; p=0.015; LA-EAT: HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.99-1.06; p=0.227). The significant association between inFAT and recurrence remained consistent after adjustment for body mass index. CONCLUSIONS: Greater inFAT volume was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF, suggesting that inFAT may represent a candidate imaging marker of recurrence risk.

recs.title: Distinguishing between nicotine replacement therapies and nicotine-containing consumer products.
Intravascular Imaging Sees Only What the Mind Is Prepared to Comprehend.
A Technique for Slack Formation During Proximal Left Bundle Branch Pacing With a Lumenless Defibrillation Lead.
Remote Blood Pressure Monitoring for Post-Acute Care and Secondary Prevention After Aortic Dissection.
Sedation and anaesthesia in pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, procedural requirements, and real-world practice.
recs.abstract: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as an important energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering tissue selectivity and procedural efficiency while introducing specific anaesthetic and sedation requirements. This narrative review examines the rationale for anaesthesia and sedation during PFA, the mechanisms underlying pain, involuntary movement, and neuromuscular stimulation, and the implications of catheter design, waveform characteristics, and patient-related factors for peri-procedural management. Available evidence indicates that both deep sedation and general anaesthesia can provide safe and effective procedural conditions when supported by appropriate monitoring, airway rescue capability, and experienced multidisciplinary teams. Deep sedation may offer advantages in workflow, recovery, and patient-centred care, particularly for standard pulmonary vein isolation procedures using contemporary biphasic systems with reduced muscle activation, whereas general anaesthesia remains appropriate for complex procedures, patients with substantial comorbidity, or settings in which complete immobility and airway control are essential. Current real-world practice is highly heterogeneous across regions and institutions, reflecting differences in regulations, staffing models, procedural complexity, and local expertise rather than a universally accepted standard. Overall, anaesthetic strategy in PFA should be individualised according to patient risk profile, expected procedural demands, and device-specific stimulation burden. Further prospective comparative studies are needed to define optimal sedation depth, standardise monitoring and outcome measures, and clarify how emerging technologies may enable lighter yet still effective sedation pathways.

recs.title: Correlation of the Distressed Communities Index Score With Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Disease in the United States.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and death worldwide. Risk scores such as the pooled cohort equations often underpredict risk in individuals with low socioeconomic status. METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Population Level Analysis and Community Estimates data set to obtain zip code-level prevalence of hypertension, obesity, stroke, diabetes, and coronary artery disease. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) collates community socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health metrics into a numerical score. Linear regression adjusted for region and rurality assessed associations between DCI and CVD prevalence. RESULTS: We included 26 058 US zip codes (2016-2020). The median DCI was 50.9 (interquartile range, 25.4-75.9). Each 1-unit increase in DCI was associated with increased prevalence of obesity (β=0.10 [95% CI, 0.09-0.10]), hypertension (β=0.08 [95% CI, 0.08-0.09]), diabetes (β=0.06 [95% CI, 0.06-0.06]), coronary artery disease (β=0.03 [95% CI, 0.03-0.03]), and stroke (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.02-0.02]; all P<0.001). Rurality and region were independently associated with CVD and risk factor prevalence, with rural and southern zip codes having the highest prevalence. CONCLUSIONS: DCI, geographic region, and rurality are independently associated with greater prevalence of CVD and its risk factors in the United States. The DCI is a practical, scalable surrogate for socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health that may enhance CVD risk stratification on the basis of an area's economic resilience or disadvantage. Using DCI with the Preventing Cardiovascular Events score may capture economic and social challenges it omits, warranting further study.
